title: Bitcoin Whales Add 121,117 BTC as Price Falls Nearly 30%
summary: Bitcoin addresses holding 1,000 to 10,000 BTC added 121,117 BTC in the first 52 days of the fourth quarter as bitcoin fell 29.5%, Cryptoquant found.
content:
Bitcoin addresses holding 1,000 to 10,000 BTC added 121,117 BTC in the first 52 days of the fourth quarter as bitcoin fell 29.5%, Cryptoquant found. Addresses holding at least 1,000 BTC recorded $2.1 billion in net realized losses.

Key Takeaways

  • Balances rose by 121,117 BTC, the largest fourth-quarter gain since 2020.
  • Addresses with at least 1,000 BTC booked $2.1 billion in net losses.
  • Whale-sized exchange inflows averaged 3,955 BTC a day in Q4.

Whale Balances Rise During Bitcoin’s Fourth-Quarter Slide

Bitcoin addresses holding 1,000 to 10,000 BTC increased their combined balance to 2.95 million BTC from Sept. 30 to Nov. 21, according to Cryptoquant’s fourth-quarter whale analysis, published Nov. 27 with support from crypto lender Coinrabbit. Bitcoin fell to about $55,000 on Nov. 21.

Cryptoquant wrote:

“Balances in the 1k–10k BTC cohort are up 121,117 BTC since Sep 30 while price fell 29.5%.”

The report noted: “The cohort of addresses with a balance of 1k–10k BTC has shed coins in seven of nine Q4s since 2017.”

Holdings rose 4.29%, the biggest fourth-quarter gain in BTC terms since 2020, after declining by 202,981 BTC in the fourth quarter of 2025. At the same point in the fourth quarters of 2018 and 2022, balances had fallen 0.06% and 1.29%, respectively. Addresses holding 100 to 1,000 BTC shed 15,169 BTC this quarter through Nov. 21.

Cryptoquant had put holdings for a broader group at 3.03 million BTC in October. That measure covered holders of at least 1,000 BTC and excluded exchange and mining pool addresses.

A single holder can control several addresses, and a custodian can hold coins for multiple customers. That distinction affects how analysts track large bitcoin holdings and interpret changes in the combined balances of addresses in a size group.

Whale Losses Mount as Exchange Inflows Pick Up

Addresses holding at least 1,000 BTC realized net losses averaging $41 million a day through Nov. 21. In the fourth quarters from 2019 through 2025, the group averaged $131 million a day in net gains. October remained profitable at $66 million a day, before November swung to a daily net loss of $197 million through the cutoff.

Unrealized gains for addresses holding at least 1,000 BTC fell to $23.8 billion from $124.7 billion at the end of September. The unrealized profit margin for the 1,000-to-10,000 BTC group sank to a 2026 low of 5.7% from 33.9%. Earlier in November, Cryptoquant market analyst Darkfost estimated that short-term whales’ paper losses totaled nearly $8 billion for coins acquired within the previous 155 days.

Cryptoquant added:

“Selling now locks in a thin gain or a loss, yet unlike 2018 and 2022 the whale cohort is still adding coins.”

Exchange inflows from unspent transaction outputs of at least 1,000 BTC rose to 5,012 BTC a day in November from 3,239 BTC in October. The quarter-to-date average of 3,955 BTC a day remained below the 2019-2025 fourth-quarter average of 4,575 BTC. Whale-sized transfers accounted for 9.9% of all exchange inflows, down from 10.8% in January through September.

During the November sell-off, wallets linked to London hedge fund Abraxas Capital Management received about 17,597 BTC from Binance and Kraken. The withdrawals increased the firm’s tracked balances during the downturn. The transfers alone leave the terms of any underlying trades unknown.

Large Borrowers Take More BTC Loans as Volume Falls

Among Coinrabbit customers with more than $100,000 in loans, the number of BTC loans rose 298.9% from September to October while loan volume fell 16.2%. In October 2025, loan count fell 3.7% while volume rose 122.8%. Cryptoquant did not link those borrowers’ accounts to the addresses in its whale analysis.

The number of loans per customer in the group rose 6.9% in October while volume per customer fell 37.3%. Borrowing against bitcoin can provide cash without selling the collateral. Interest adds to the cost, and a falling bitcoin price can trigger liquidation.

Crypto tax software provider Summ suggested that wider tax reporting could encourage large holders to defer sales, borrow against bitcoin, or realize losses for tax purposes. Summ presented those potential incentives as an interpretation of the data. The Global Forum of the Organization for Economic Cooperation and Development expects the first cross-border crypto tax data exchanges in September 2027.

title: XRP Deposits on Binance Outnumber Withdrawals More Than 11 to 1
summary: XRP deposits accounted for 91.4% of tracked deposit and withdrawal transactions on Binance over seven days, the highest share since 2019. Across all
content:
1. News
  2. Market Updates
  3. XRP Deposits on Binance Outnumber Withdrawals More Than 11 to 1

Published:Nov 27, 2026, 9:40 PM EST

XRP deposits accounted for 91.4% of tracked deposit and withdrawal transactions on Binance over seven days, the highest share since 2019. Across all exchanges in the analysis, deposits and withdrawals were nearly even.

WRITTEN BY

SHARE

Published: Nov 27, 2026, 9:40 PM EST

Key Takeaways

  • Binance recorded 11.4 XRP deposit transactions for every withdrawal.
  • Deposits made up 49% of XRP transfers across tracked exchanges.
  • Binance’s XRP futures volume was about 4.6 times its spot volume.

Binance’s XRP Deposit Share Reaches Its Highest Since 2019

Binance recorded more than 11 XRP deposit transactions for every withdrawal over the seven days through Nov. 26, according to Amr Taha’s exchange transaction analysis. The Cryptoquant contributor put the deposit share at 91.4% and the withdrawal share at 8% as XRP traded near $0.95.

The analyst wrote:

“Deposit transactions outnumbered withdrawals by 11.4 times, compared with 4.55 times in May 2019, when deposits and withdrawals accounted for 81.9% and 18%, respectively. The current ratio is approximately 151% higher.”

The latest split reversed a withdrawal-heavy pattern seen on Binance earlier this year. During a seven-day stretch of withdrawal dominance that began June 17, XRP withdrawals consistently outnumbered deposits. On the June 23 reading, withdrawals accounted for 53.8% of transactions, while deposits made up 46.1%.

Deposits and Withdrawals Stay Nearly Even Across Exchanges

Across the exchanges the analysis tracked, the deposit share rose from 44% on Oct. 27 to 49% on Nov. 27, while the withdrawal share fell from 55% to 50%. Kucoin’s deposit share was about 74%. Most other exchanges fell between 45% and 55%.

The deposit share gives each transfer equal weight regardless of size. In its daily exchange wallet flow data, XRP Sonar recorded a net inflow of 4.7 million XRP to known Binance wallets on Nov. 26. Across the exchanges it tracked, 91.5 million XRP left and 80.8 million XRP arrived.

Binance restored access in phases after its October security breach. By Nov. 14, the exchange had reopened withdrawals across 87 networks and said it aimed to restore withdrawals on the remaining networks the following week.

The exchange said on Nov. 26 that the withdrawal suspension tied to the breach had been fully lifted. Binance still had temporary pauses on a small number of networks undergoing maintenance or planned upgrades.

XRP Futures Volume Still Exceeds Spot Trading

Binance’s XRP spot volume reached 21.8% of futures volume on Nov. 26, up from 19.4% in September and below 27.2% on Nov. 4. Futures volume was about 4.6 times spot volume on Nov. 26.

Trading volume measures the value of completed trades over a given period. The spot and futures figures reflect activity in those two markets, while the deposit share tracks how often XRP moved into Binance wallets.

The analyst identified spot trading as a measure to watch if holders sold the XRP they deposited. The ratio tracks spot volume relative to futures volume, so an increase can reflect more spot trading, less futures trading, or both.

Earlier XRP liquidation data on Binance showed fewer forced closures after repeated spikes from late July through September. The Nov. 27 analysis put the largest estimated long liquidation cluster at $0.85 and the largest short liquidation cluster at $1.05.

About the author

WRITTEN BYKevin Helms

Kevin Helms is a cryptocurrency journalist specializing in Bitcoin, blockchain regulation, and global digital asset markets.

title: ASEAN, Japan, China and South Korea Launch Cross-Border Payments Task Force
summary: Learn about ASEAN's initiative to develop cross-border domestic payment systems and boost regional economic cooperation.
content:
1. News
  2. Finance
  3. ASEAN, Japan, China and South Korea Launch Cross-Border Payments Task Force

Published:Nov 27, 2026, 8:25 PM EST

The organization of Southeast Asian countries plus Japan, China, and South Korea will form a working group to implement an integrated policy to deal with these problems and simplify the expansion of domestic payment methods to an international level. Details will be revealed next year at the Nagoya ASEAN+3 gathering.

WRITTEN BY

SHARE

Published: Nov 27, 2026, 8:25 PM EST

Key Takeaways

  • ASEAN+3 officials agreed to form a working group to make domestic payment systems work across borders.
  • Expanding local payment methods drives regional de-dollarization and lowers cross-border transaction costs.
  • The push could integrate CBDCs like China’s digital yuan, expanding Beijing’s leverage in regional trade.

ASEAN+3 Group Forms Working Group To Organize Digital Payments Initiatives

The Association of Southeast Asian Nations plus three (ASEAN+3), a regional group that brings together Southeast Asian nations with Japan, China, and South Korea, has given a hint to its upcoming digital payments strategy.

According to Reuters, at a meeting in Kyoto, deputies to finance ministers ​and central bank governors from the organization agreed to coordinate a working group to develop a joint payment policy ensuring the interoperability of existing payment methods across the region.

The working group that will be formed aims to expand payment methods originally designed for domestic operations to work internationally, highlighting the need to overhaul current international settlement methods.

A mechanism to allow access to emergency funds to tackle pandemic and emergency-disaster-derived shocks was discussed as part of a $240 billion currency swap known as the Chiang Mai Initiative, launched in May 2000 for member countries to leverage during liquidity crunch periods. More details will be revealed at the next ASEAN+3 Finance Ministers and Central Bank Governors Meeting in May 2027.

Focusing on domestic payment methods ensures payment policies will involve local currencies, supporting the group’s de-dollarization push outlined since 2023 and accelerated by the surge of unilateral U.S. sanctions against Russia.

In 2025, Brunei, Cambodia, Indonesia, Laos, Malaysia, Myanmar, the Philippines, Singapore, Thailand, and Vietnam outlined their currency sovereignty strategy in the Economic Community Strategic Plan 2026–2030, released on May 26 during the 46th ASEAN Summit.

In the document, the organization states it will “promote the use of local currencies to reduce the region’s vulnerability to exchange rate fluctuations and external economic and financial shocks, and to lower transaction costs associated with cross-border payments.”

A February International Monetary Fund (IMF) paper found that cross-border digital payments can promote local currency usage and facilitate regional trade and financial integration among ASEAN countries, with Thailand leading the transition to digital cross-border payments.

Digital payments can also take advantage of central bank digital currencies, such as the digital yuan, providing China with some leverage across the region given the size and scope of its economy.

In 2023, the Chinese Region of Guanxi highlighted the possibilities of integrating the digital yuan for trade settlements across ASEAN, aiming to internationalize the digital currency that was in its initial stages at the time.

About the author

WRITTEN BYSergio Goschenko

Sergio is a cryptocurrency journalist based in Venezuela with 2,000+ articles published, cited in dozens of papers and reports.

title: Vitalik Buterin’s Bitcoin Hardware Wallet Fix Wouldn’t Be Approved by Ledger CTO
summary: Vitalik Buterin proposes open-source hardware security for bitcoin wallets, but Ledger's CTO previously called the idea wishful thinking.
content:
In a terrible year for hardware wallet users and manufacturers, Ethereum co-founder Vitalik Buterin has proposed a fix aimed mainly at tampered chips, a threat that hasn’t caused known losses yet. Parts of his proposal are already being tested in products, but it wouldn’t make these wallets completely trustless.

Key Takeaways

  • Vitalik Buterin argues that secure hardware should be open and inspectable down to the factory drawings, even at the cost of efficiency.
  • Ledger CTO Charles Guillemet disagrees, arguing that open-source chip designs cannot guarantee that actual hardware matches the published specifications.
  • A layered security approach combining open- and closed-source components offers a middle ground between hardware transparency and protection against attacks, but it doesn’t eliminate the need for trust.

Buterin discussed his solution in his Nov. 26 post, “A shallow dive into open-source chip design,” reminding hardware wallet users that owning your private keys isn’t enough if you can’t trust the chip that secures them:

“Not your silicon, not your keys.”

‘Performance Hardware’ and ‘Secure Hardware’

He argues that secure chips, including those in hardware wallets, must be open all the way down to the factory drawings so independent specialists can compare actual chips with the designs, even though such hardware may be much less efficient.

According to Buterin, professional auditors, journalists, and civil society groups could audit manufacturers and distributors. Chips could be inspected by photographing their insides with infrared light, but detecting subtler tampering often requires taking a chip apart layer by layer, destroying it in the process. This means only samples could undergo a full inspection, not the chip in your wallet. Buterin adds that chips also need to be designed to be “more inspection-friendly.”

“In order for computation to be democratized, the hardware layer must be open for participation and tinkering too. In order for computation to be secure, the hardware layer must be open and inspectable,” Buterin concluded, forecasting that the hardware industry will split into “performance hardware” and “secure hardware” categories. The latter, according to Buterin, may be 10x less efficient or more, “but it will be efficient enough for almost everything we care to do.”

Elegant Wishful Thinking

The debate over open-source design in bitcoin and crypto hardware wallets has been going on for years, and manufacturers take different approaches. During the Coldcard crisis this summer, for example, wallets with stronger open-source credentials, such as Trezor, Bitbox, and Blockstream Jade, leaned on verifiability, while more closed designs, such as Ledger, relied on certifications and audits. Buterin’s point, however, concerns open-sourcing the hardware itself. This is where Ledger CTO Charles Guillemet, who is leaving the company at the end of the year, disagrees.

In August, he argued that open source is not a security property and that there is no way to prove that a published chip design matches the actual chip you buy.

“You might think: ‘Then build an open-source secure element.’ That sounds elegant. It is mostly wishful thinking,” Guillemet said, emphasizing that “many eyes” checking the code doesn’t guarantee security, as the Coldcard catastrophe showed. As reported by Bitcoin.com News, Coldcard’s manufacturer Coinkite claims that its randomness bug sat in publicly available code for more than five years and was missed by at least 15 independent security research and review efforts.

According to the departing CTO, closed source is what makes exploitation harder: “Anyone who has done offensive security knows this.”

Hardware hacker Andrew “bunnie” Huang, whose infrared inspection method Buterin cites, has described the industry’s usual model: users hand their trust to vendors, so “anti-tamper measures take priority over inspectability.” Huang himself works from the opposite assumption: no vendor can be trusted. In short, Ledger’s approach mainly protects against whoever gets hold of a device, while Buterin’s mainly focuses on whoever made it.

Combining Open- and Closed-Source Designs

However, as with many things, the choice between open- and closed-source hardware wallet designs isn’t black and white. For example, Trezor Safe 7 already combines a certified, closed chip (Infineon OPTIGA), the open-design TROPIC01 chip, made by Trezor’s sister company Tropic Square, and the main microcontroller. According to Trezor, the seed isn’t stored in either secure chip. Instead, it’s encrypted on the main microcontroller using keys from both TROPIC01 and OPTIGA.

Meanwhile, a security test of TROPIC01 this year offered some support for both hardware-wallet competitors’ arguments. In a lab, researchers from Ledger’s Donjon team used a laser to bypass the chip’s firmware signature check, which let them run their own code on the chip and, Trezor says, extract a subset of the secrets it protects. They said the published code showed them exactly how the check worked and which step to target.

However, Trezor’s argument also stands: the flaw was disclosed publicly, a fix for future chips is in the works, and Trezor says the layered design means the flaw alone can’t expose users’ PINs or funds. The question remains how many other layers attackers might bypass in the future, if any.

The Trust Problem

Either way, chip flaws weren’t behind the actual incidents this year. Coldcard’s weak seed generation was caused by a firmware bug, while the implants found in Ledger and, on a smaller scale, Trezor devices were extra parts added inside the cases. Buterin discusses a potential future attack vector: chips swapped for look-alikes. He warns that hardware-wallet manufacturers should start preparing for this possibility now.

A better way to ensure that hardware hasn’t been tampered with during manufacturing—and remains unchanged until it reaches the user—may eventually emerge. In 2023, bunnie suggested checking a chip first and then, if tamper resistance is needed, sealing it in opaque epoxy to protect it from subsequent tampering.

However, whether hardware wallet users will ever reach a point where they don’t need to trust anyone at all remains an open question.

title: Injective Urges SEC to Open Tokenized Stock Trading to Order Books
summary: Injective has urged the U.S. SEC to expand its tokenized stock trading exemptions to include on-chain order books.
content:
Injective has urged the U.S. SEC to expand its tokenized stock trading exemptions to include onchain order books. The proposal challenges existing restrictions that favor automated liquidity pools, potentially opening new opportunities for crypto platforms and traditional investors.

Key Takeaways

  • Injective’s third SEC submission seeks tokenized stock exemptions for on-chain order books.
  • The proposal includes safeguards against market manipulation and front-running.
  • SEC approval could expand competition and improve onchain price discovery.

Injective Challenges SEC Rules Favoring Crypto Liquidity Pools

Injective is challenging a key limitation in U.S. crypto regulation, arguing that blockchain-based stock exchanges should receive equal treatment regardless of how they match trades.

In a 22-page policy letter dated Nov. 23, Injective Labs asked the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) to extend its exemption for tokenized equities to onchain order books, the trading model underpinning traditional stock markets.

The SEC’s existing five-year exemption, introduced in September, permits qualifying tokenized stock trading through automated market makers (AMMs) and liquidity pools. Order book-based platforms remain excluded.

Injective argues that this distinction could restrict competition as financial institutions increasingly explore blockchain-based securities trading.

Injective Challenges SEC’s Tokenized Stock Trading Restrictions

The company contends that onchain orderbooks offer the same fundamental benefits that persuaded regulators to approve exemptions for AMMs.

These include round-the-clock trading, self-custody, near-instant settlement, and publicly verifiable transactions.

In its submission, Injective argued that “the exemption should turn on the characteristics and safeguards of the onchain venue,” rather than its trading mechanism.

Orderbooks also display bids, offers, and available liquidity, potentially improving price discovery and helping tokenized stock prices remain aligned with conventional markets.

Unlike AMMs, they do not require separate liquidity pools, potentially reducing certain risks for retail liquidity providers.

Investor Protections Take Center Stage in Third SEC Appeal

Injective proposed additional safeguards to address concerns about manipulation and market integrity. These include mandatory market surveillance, self-trade prevention, price limits, and protocol-level trading halts.

The company also highlighted its frequent batch auction mechanism, which can reduce front-running and maximum extractable value (MEV) risks by processing eligible orders under predetermined matching rules.

The latest letter marks Injective’s third formal policy submission to the SEC, following earlier recommendations concerning decentralized finance and onchain lending. Injective is seeking broader regulatory changes rather than an exemption exclusively for its own blockchain.

The outcome could influence how U.S. investors access tokenized equities and how crypto platforms compete to bring traditional financial markets onchain.

For now, the SEC has yet to approve the proposed expansion.

title: Here’s what happened in crypto today
summary: Need to know what happened in crypto today? Here is the latest news on daily trends and events impacting Bitcoin price, blockchain, DeFi, Web3 and crypto regulation.
content:
Today in crypto, Bitcoin whales have added about 121,000 BTC since the end of September, defying historical year-end selling patterns. Meanwhile, the EU’s securities watchdog plans to make it easier to verify which crypto companies are authorized to operate in the bloc, and crypto bug bounty platforms are expanding their use of AI to identify genuine security threats amid a surge in submissions.

Bitcoin whales pile into BTC despite shrinking profit cushion

Bitcoin whales are bucking the years-long trend of trimming their balances toward the end of the year. Instead, they are accumulating the cryptocurrency despite falling prices and dwindling unrealized profits.

According to onchain analytics firm CryptoQuant, whales added about 121,000 Bitcoin (BTC) to their holdings between Sept. 30 and Nov. 21, taking their combined balance to nearly 2.95 million BTC, despite a price decline of nearly 30% over the same period.

CryptoQuant defines whales as addresses holding between 1,000 and 10,000 BTC. Unrealized profits across addresses holding at least 1,000 BTC have shrunk 81% to $23.8 billion from $124.7 billion on Sept. 30.

The report, supported by crypto lending platform CoinRabbit, notes that whales have historically reduced their holdings toward the end of the year in both bull and bear markets. Since 2017, whale balances have declined in seven of the nine previous fourth quarters, with 2019 and 2020 being the only exceptions.

Meanwhile, dolphins, a term referring to addresses holding between 100 and 1,000 BTC, have slightly reduced their holdings. The group shed about 15,169 BTC, representing 0.28% of its holdings.

ESMA to overhaul EU’s MiCA crypto register in 2027

The European Securities and Markets Authority (ESMA) is preparing an overhaul of its public crypto register nearly two years after its launch.

The European Union’s securities watchdog plans to replace its manual interim register under the Markets in Crypto-Assets Regulation (MiCA) with a searchable web-based platform around mid-2027, an ESMA spokesperson told Cointelegraph.

The new system will also maintain a version history for individual white papers to provide archives of changes.

MiCA’s transitional period ended in July, which meant that unauthorized crypto service providers had to wind down their EU operations or face multimillion-euro fines or other enforcement action. ESMA’s interim register serves as a public reference point for checking whether a crypto company is authorized in the bloc.

AI is driving a flood of crypto bug reports. Now it’s helping sort them

Crypto bug bounty platforms have expanded their use of artificial intelligence to keep up with a growing mountain of AI-assisted security reports.

Crypto-focused HackenProof said in October that it was using AI to triage 70% of submissions fully autonomously, aiming to hit 85% by the end of 2026. It said it received an average of about 6,100 bug reports a month in the third quarter, 2.4 times the reports from December last year.

Rival Immunefi last week said submissions to its platform rose 136% year-over-year in the first nine months of 2026, as it introduced a tool that can flag duplicates before a researcher submits a report.

Bug bounty programs pay independent researchers to find and report potential security flaws. AI has helped researchers uncover more genuine vulnerabilities, but has also swelled the volume of invalid and duplicate submissions, making it harder for security teams to identify the threats that need urgent attention.

It’s like “bringing a sword to a gunfight,” Dmitry Tokarev, founder of crypto wallet provider Bron, told Cointelegraph, referring to security teams that haven’t already adopted AI to sift through reports.

title: Ethereum Developers Set December Glamsterdam Test Despite Smart Contract Concerns
summary: Ethereum’s long-delayed network upgrade will undergo another round of testing in December despite concerns over disrupted smart contracts.
content:
Ethereum’s long-delayed network upgrade will undergo another round of testing in December despite concerns that proposed gas pricing changes could disrupt thousands of smart contracts.

Key Takeaways

  • Ethereum developers agreed to activate Glamsterdam on the Hoodi testnet on Dec. 15 despite lingering smart contract compatibility concerns.
  • Proposed gas pricing changes could affect existing smart contracts that power crypto apps, bridges, and platforms, though developers maintain that the changes are necessary to scale Ethereum without sacrificing decentralization.
  • Ethereum developers also debated prioritizing quantum-resistant cryptography in the subsequent Hegota upgrade.

Ethereum developers are moving forward with the blockchain’s ambitious Glamsterdam upgrade after weeks of delays, opting to retain controversial changes to the network’s gas pricing mechanism despite warnings that thousands of existing smart contracts could be disrupted.

Participants in Thursday’s All Core Developers Consensus (ACDC) call agreed to activate Glamsterdam on Ethereum’s Hoodi testnet on Dec. 15 at 19:12 UTC. Teams responsible for Ethereum’s execution and consensus layer software are expected to have updated releases ready early next week, according to a summary from Ethereum Magicians.

The upcoming test comes nearly two months after developers abandoned their original Oct. 26 activation plans following the discovery of potentially serious smart contract compatibility issues.

Ethereum Pushes Ahead With Glamsterdam

At the heart of the debate is Ethereum Improvement Proposal (EIP) 8037, which increases the amount of gas required for operations that expand the blockchain’s permanent database. The measure is designed to help Ethereum accommodate substantially more transactions without dramatically increasing the hardware requirements for running a node.

However, applications built around Ethereum’s existing gas pricing structure could malfunction once the changes take effect, particularly if their smart contracts allocate fixed amounts of gas to certain operations.

As previously reported by Bitcoin.com News, ChainSecurity initially identified 13 deployed contracts in October that exhibited particularly concerning behavior under Glamsterdam’s proposed gas rules. In certain instances, operations that would ordinarily fail and allow users to try again could instead leave contracts in an irreversible state, potentially preventing users from accessing funds.

Last week, ChainSecurity said it has now found 200 potential issues, with three of them ranked “high” severity but none elevated to “critical” status.

Ethereum co-founder Vitalik Buterin defended EIP-8037 earlier this month, arguing that the network must distinguish between the costs of processing transactions and permanently storing data if it is to scale without sacrificing decentralization. Buterin acknowledged the compatibility challenges but warned that further alterations could introduce new problems and stall other development priorities.

Ethereum’s Next Upgrades

Glamsterdam represents one of Ethereum’s most substantial planned overhauls since its 2022 transition to proof-of-stake, a.k.a. the “merge.” The upgrade introduces changes to how blocks are constructed and validated, alongside improvements that facilitate parallel transaction processing.

Developers have targeted an increase in Ethereum’s per-block gas limit from 60 million to 200 million, with October testing on the Sepolia testnet demonstrating the feasibility of operating near that higher threshold. Originally anticipated during the first half of 2026, Glamsterdam now appears likely to reach Ethereum mainnet in early 2027, barring further testing issues.

Meanwhile, Thursday’s developer call also highlighted growing debate over Ethereum’s subsequent upgrade, Hegota, as researchers weigh accelerating the network’s transition to quantum-resistant cryptography.

Some developers advocated dropping Fork Choice Enforced Inclusion Lists (FOCIL), a proposed mechanism for improving Ethereum’s censorship resistance, to free up development resources for post-quantum security. Others maintained that both initiatives could advance concurrently.

Developers are expected to revisit Hegota’s proposed features during their next consensus call around Dec. 10, just days before Glamsterdam’s scheduled Hoodi activation.

title: Franklin Templeton makes room for HYPE in crypto index ETF
summary: The addition comes as US spot investment products tracking Hyperliquid’s native token reach $266.5 million in assets under management.
content:
Asset manager Franklin Templeton plans to add the Hyperliquid (HYPE) token to its crypto index exchange-traded fund (ETF), according to a filing with the US Securities and Exchange Commission on Nov. 25.

The token will be added to the Franklin Crypto Index ETF on Dec. 1, following HYPE’s inclusion in the fund’s benchmark. The fund, which trades under the ticker EZPZ, currently holds Bitcoin (BTC), Ether (ETH), XRP, Solana (SOL), Dogecoin (DOGE), Cardano (ADA) and Lumen (XLM).

Hyperliquid, a layer-1 blockchain that hosts a decentralized exchange specializing in perpetual futures trading, has seen its total value locked rise to $7.3 billion from $4.13 billion in early January. The protocol generated $80.3 million in revenue over the past 30 days, according to DefiLlama.

Its native token, HYPE, is used to pay network fees and can be staked to earn rewards. The protocol also uses a portion of its trading fee revenue to buy back HYPE on the open market, linking trading activity on the platform to demand for the token.

Related: HYPE teases all-time high as NYSE owner ICE eyes US Hyperliquid perps

HYPE expands its Wall Street footprint

Franklin Templeton’s move comes as more investment products offer exposure to HYPE.

Three US spot exchange-traded products (ETPs) tracking HYPE have launched since May, with offerings from asset managers 21Shares, Bitwise and Grayscale. They collectively held approximately $266.5 million in assets under management as of Nov. 27, according to Coinperps data.

These products allow US investors to gain exposure to the Hyperliquid ecosystem through traditional financial rails without having to directly hold the token.

The exchange ranks among the largest venues for decentralized perpetual futures trading, although its official interface remains restricted to US users. Perpetual futures are derivative contracts that allow traders to speculate on an asset’s price movements without a fixed expiration date.

President Donald Trump said in August that Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) Chair Michael Selig was working to bring Hyperliquid into the US in compliance with regulations.

Related: Hong Kong adds Hyperliquid to list of ‘suspicious’ crypto platforms

title: Silver Price Analysis: XAG/USD Faces Deeper Losses as $40 Support Nears
summary: After Silver's latest sell-off, the question for the trader is whether or not they can hold the $40 level and stave off further losses in the market.
content:
Skip to content
Assets: XAG

After Silver's latest sell-off, the question for the trader is whether or not they can hold the $40 level and stave off further losses in the market.

The week’s fall in silver prices highlights the fragility of the market. This week’s slide in silver prices is a sign of the market’s fragility.

Silver’s Weekly Decline Exposes a Weakening Market

Silver has continued its downward trend, falling 15.37% over the past week to around $41.23 per ounce, as seen on the Trading Economics chart.

The Investing.com daily chart also shows silver lost 3.86% during the session, ending around $41.20 after the lowest price it hit during today’s session was $40.77.

The higher-level chart pattern indicates a long-term return from the August highs around $70. Source: TradingEconomics

Since then, successive lower highs and lower lows have been observed, suggesting that sellers have been in control. The drop was picked up after the metal’s recovery in November collapsed, taking the price back towards the $53 mark.

The price is in line with the overall decline of precious metals. The drop in gold and silver prices was blamed in a November 21 Wall Street Journal report on rising interest rates for U.S. government bonds and a stronger U.S. dollar and on additional rate increases by the Federal Reserve. Silver’s industrial ties make it a weak performer when investors are nervous about economic growth, too.

Technical Outlook: $40 Becomes the Next Major Test

The daily chart shows a bearish pattern with the price of silver moving into the lower part of the range shown and near the bottom of the daily consolidation range. The first significant support reference is the latest session’s low at $40.77. The next psychological level that traders should pay attention to is $40 below.

However, if silver continues to close below $40 every day, it could bring additional downside pressure to silver and further confirm the ongoing series of lower lows. But if there is a temporary drop below support with a fast bounce up, it might mean that the buyers are trying to cover the selling pressure.

According to the chart, the positive side is that 42.80–43.60 seems to be a point of initial resistance as per the opening and higher levels of the recent daily trading session. Source: investing.com

If the price can resume its recovery from this area, it may resume its move toward $45, where there was some selling pressure previously. A wider range of resistance is seen in the $47-48 zone, a previous consolidation area before the prior breakdown.

All other technical evidence is negative. In its technical summary for November, Investing.com said silver is a “strong sell” as the RSI was below the neutral 50 level and the majority of moving averages indicated selling pressure.

What Traders Should Watch Next?

The first question that needs to be asked is if silver can sustain the $40 support level during a resumption of trading. If prices fall below it, then the bearish argument would be reinforced, and if they rise above it, perhaps for the first time, it would suggest that selling pressure is easing.

US dollar, Treasury yields, and Federal Reserve communications should also be watched by traders. Any further improvement in yields and a stronger dollar will remain a headwind for non-yielding precious metals. However, if the economy releases weaker data or the policy stance is less hawkish, there will be a chance to recover.

Industrial-demand expectations are also an element to consider, as silver is used in the manufacturing sector as well as the monetary market. Even if gold stabilizes, the prospects for buying will be constrained by signs of weaker industrial activity.

The technical picture is currently tilted towards sellers. For traders to assert that the recent pullback is over, they must get some of that nearby resistance cleared before the big move to the downside resumes. Until then, the $40 level is the key price to look at for a possible stabilization versus another leg lower.

title: Lithium Price Outlook as Sellers Target 80,000 Yuan After Failed Recovery
summary: Lithium recovery stutters as oversupply weighs on China's carbonate market.
content:
Skip to content
Assets: Li

Lithium recovery stutters as oversupply weighs on China's carbonate market.

Excess supply has dragged down prices from 2026 peaks, while soft new offers drove futures towards 80,000 yuan a tonne.

According to market data, there is renewed hesitation among buyers after an attempted recovery from oversupply, even as a now-larger yawning gap between past peaks and current levels begs the question of where the market might find its next bottom.

LITHIUM FUTURES RETREAT AS SELLERS DEFEND 84,000 YUAN LEVEL

The X update illustrates lithium carbonate futures trying but failing to maintain an attempted bounce. The Jan LC2701 contract was at 82,100 yuan a tonne, down 2.47% for the session.

The analyst chart shows the contract opened at 84,000 yuan and hit 85,100 yuan during trading. Source: Carl Via X

Prices were driven by sellers down to 82,080 yuan, near the bottom of the session. Trading volume was 199,813 lots; open interest was 324,382 lots.

The bearish reversal from 85,100 yuan indicates momentum buyers are no longer driving the market higher. The 84,000-yuan opening mark may serve as initial resistance. If the market recovers above 85,100 yuan, that would be a better sign of fresh buying support.

For now, 82,080 yuan is support, and a firm close below it is likely to test the 80,000-yuan psychological level. Capolingua analysis also indicates the presence of excess supply and may still be on the rally to the seller.

TRADING ECONOMICS SHOWS A PROLONGED PRICE DECLINE

Trading Economics’ chart over a year shows lithium carbonate tumbling from around 200,000 yuan per tonne in May to 86,100 yuan as of 26 November. That’s a big correction since the top of the year.

The chart shows a series of failed recoveries in the second half of 2026. Source: Trading Economics

A failed rally towards 140,000 yuan in August was followed by a rally to 160,000 yuan in September. A renewed selling bout saw the market accelerate through October and November.

86,100 is the most recent reading, which is a year-over-year decrease of 7.72%. The previous region at 90,000 yuan offers a key rebound benchmark, and between 95,000 and 100,000 yuan are higher thresholds. A concerted break above these areas would signal a pickup in price momentum.

The psychological level of 80,000 yuan still acts as a key downside reference. However, the chart hasn’t formed a confirmed reversal or a reliable price support.

The broader market backdrop also encourages restraint. Trading Economics cites abundant supply, higher inventories, and a softer demand outlook.

WHAT LITHIUM INVESTORS SHOULD WATCH NEXT

Investors should observe whether LC2701 is able to hold at 82,080 yuan or if it tests down to 80,000 yuan. On the upside, the resistance zone to recover to is 84,000–85,100 yuan. Keep an eye on spot-market deals, battery manufacturer procurement, and inventory trends.

China’s lithium spodumene imports above one million tonnes in October prompted more worries about raw-material availability. Stable lithium prices can be underpinned by sustained tight supply or relatively resilient downstream procurement.

When it comes to supply, the relatively slower restarting of spodumene mines and solid low-end battery-sector demand may linger at this stage.

title: Bitcoin Price Could Hit $400K by 2030, Coinbase CEO Brian Armstrong Says
summary: Coinbase CEO Brian Armstrong believes bitcoin has likely reached its current market bottom and could climb to $400,000 by 2030.
content:
Coinbase CEO Brian Armstrong believes the price of bitcoin has likely reached its current market bottom and could climb to $400,000 by 2030. He also revealed that AI-powered trading on Coinbase is growing 20% weekly as the exchange expands its financial services.

Key Takeaways

  • Brian Armstrong believes bitcoin has bottomed and could hit $400K by 2030.
  • Newer financial products now generate 25% of Coinbase’s trading fees.
  • AI trading is growing 20% weekly, opening new opportunities in automated finance.

Armstrong Sees Bitcoin Recovery as Coinbase Expands Beyond Crypto

Bitcoin’s recent sell-off may have run its course, according to Coinbase CEO Brian Armstrong, who expects the cryptocurrency to recover from recent levels near $60,000 and potentially reach $400,000 within four years.

Speaking during an interview with WOLF Financial at Tomorrow X, Armstrong expressed confidence in bitcoin’s long-term prospects despite recent market turbulence.

“I think we’ve probably seen the bottom on this one,” Armstrong said, adding that bitcoin could reach “$400,000 or more” by 2030.

Armstrong linked bitcoin’s recent weakness partly to market activity surrounding Anthropic’s initial public offering, suggesting the resulting pressure could prove temporary. He argued that bitcoin’s latest cycle bottom remains approximately four times higher than the previous cycle’s low, reinforcing his optimism for the coming year.

Meanwhile, Coinbase is expanding beyond cryptocurrency trading into stocks, derivatives, and prediction markets.

Armstrong revealed that approximately 25% of its trading fees now come from prediction markets, derivatives, and other newer products. The expansion reflects Coinbase’s ambition to reshape traditional finance through tokenized equities, around-the-clock trading, and broader access to financial services.

Coinbase AI Trading Jumps 20% Weekly as Security Takes Priority

Artificial intelligence represents another major growth opportunity.

Armstrong revealed that AI-powered trading activity on Coinbase is increasing 20% week-over-week as customers deploy automated agents to manage investments. The company is developing financial accounts, payment infrastructure, and marketplaces for AI agents, allowing users to automate portfolio adjustments, tax-loss harvesting, and trading strategies.

Armstrong said users retain control through spending restrictions, approval requirements, and segregated funds. He also advocated decentralized AI development to prevent excessive concentration of technological power.

On cybersecurity, Armstrong said Coinbase uses specialized AI agents to review production code and stores more than 99% of customer funds offline. He cited relationships with seven major banks, 140 government institutions, and 50 leading hedge funds as evidence of the company’s institutional reach.

Armstrong also discussed Coinbase’s response to an attempted extortion scheme last year, including offering a reward for information leading to the attackers’ arrest and cooperating with law enforcement.

With crypto adoption expanding, Armstrong believes automated finance and stronger security will increasingly shape the industry’s future.

title: Bitcoin whales pile into BTC despite shrinking profit cushion
summary: CryptoQuant data shows Bitcoin whales are breaking with historical fourth-quarter selling patterns despite a market downturn.
content:
Bitcoin whales are bucking the years-long trend of trimming their balances toward the end of the year. Instead, they are accumulating the cryptocurrency despite falling prices and dwindling unrealized profits.

According to onchain analytics firm CryptoQuant, whales added about 121,000 Bitcoin (BTC) to their holdings between Sept. 30 and Nov. 21, taking their combined balance to nearly 2.95 million BTC, despite a price decline of nearly 30% over the same period.

CryptoQuant defines whales as addresses holding between 1,000 and 10,000 BTC. Unrealized profits across addresses holding at least 1,000 BTC have shrunk 81% to $23.8 billion from $124.7 billion on Sept. 30.

The report, supported by crypto lending platform CoinRabbit, notes that whales have historically reduced their holdings toward the end of the year in both bull and bear markets. Since 2017, whale balances have declined in seven of the nine previous fourth quarters, with 2019 and 2020 being the only exceptions.

Meanwhile, dolphins, a term referring to addresses holding between 100 and 1,000 BTC, have slightly reduced their holdings. The group shed about 15,169 BTC, representing 0.28% of its holdings.

Related: Bitcoin supply metric hits 11-year low as new ‘capitulation’ signal arrives

Bitcoin loans may be taking the place of sales

The accumulation comes as Bitcoin has lost about 32% of its value since the beginning of the year, with the cryptocurrency trading at around $59,750 at 6:45 p.m. UTC on Friday, according to TradingView data. The report notes that borrowing against Bitcoin holdings may be allowing some large investors to access liquidity without selling their assets.

According to CryptoQuant, among CoinRabbit users with more than $100,000 in loans, the number of Bitcoin-backed loans increased by 298.9% month-on-month in October, while total loan volume fell by 16.2%.

The pattern contrasts with October 2025, when the number of Bitcoin-backed loans fell by 3.7% but total loan volume increased by 122.8%.

CryptoQuant suggested that the shift toward more frequent but smaller loans could indicate that large holders are borrowing to raise cash instead of selling Bitcoin.

Crypto tax firm Summ suggested the shift could also be linked to the Crypto-Asset Reporting Framework (CARF). Since January, participating jurisdictions have begun requiring crypto exchanges and other service providers to collect users’ transaction data for tax authorities, with the first international exchanges of tax-related information expected in 2027.

Summ CEO Shane Brunette said holding BTC and borrowing against it are rational responses “to a world where every sale is visible.”

title: Spain Moves to Freeze Crypto Accounts Without Need for Court Approval
summary: Spain enacts a new law allowing authorities to block crypto transactions for up to 10 days, enhancing financial oversight.
content:
A recently published reform to Spain’s anti-money laundering and terrorism financing prevention law allows the national financial intelligence agency to issue temporary blocks on crypto transactions for up to 10 days without a judge’s involvement.

Key Takeaways

  • Spain’s new decree lets SEPBLAC freeze suspect crypto accounts and transactions without a court order.
  • Temporary blocks last up to 10 days for transactions and five days for accounts to probe illicit fund links.
  • Set for January 2027, the EU-aligned rule accelerates Spain’s crypto oversight following Germany’s lead.

Spain Issues Decree to Allow Authorities to Freeze Crypto Accounts Without Judicial Involvement

Spain’s government has issued a new decree seeking to tighten control over fraud-linked funds, allowing authorities to take swift action on cases where illicit funds, even in the form of crypto, are leveraged.

On Wednesday, Spain’s executive issued Royal Decree-Law 44/2026, which targets consumer lending agreements and borrowers’ protection in the assignment of portfolios of non-performing loans.

The decree includes reforms to current anti-money laundering and terrorism financing prevention law, extending the powers of Spain’s financial intelligence unit in accordance with internationally proposed Financial Action Task Force (FATF) standards. It implements the EU’s 2024/1640 directive, which calls on Member States to give powers to their financial intelligence units to act immediately to suspend or withhold consent to a transaction or an account considered linked to illicit activity.

Article 46 bis, which deals with the implementation of this measure, states that the Executive Service of the Commission for the Prevention of Money Laundering and Monetary Offenses (SEPBLAC), Spain’s financial watchdog, will be able to suspend or freeze a crypto transaction or an account without a court order when signs link these to money laundering and terrorism financing activities.

The measure aims to “safeguard the funds, conduct their analyses, assess whether the suspicion is confirmed, and—if so—forward the information to the competent authorities so that they may take appropriate measures.”

The temporary blocks can extend to up to 10 days for transactions and up to five days for accounts, after which they will be lifted if no link to illicit funds is proven.

These restrictions can also be imposed at the request of law enforcement agencies, as well as upon the request of the Financial Intelligence Unit of another European Union Member State or a third state.

Spain’s move marks an acceleration of the government’s crypto-vigilance policies, after the full implementation of the Market in Crypto Assets (MiCA) framework.

These provisions will come into effect in January 2027, subject to Parliament’s approval, and follow a similar move by Germany’s Bundestag, which approved seizing cryptocurrency assets whose lawful origin is unproven for up to 180 days without a criminal investigation.

In that case, the owner of these digital assets needs to prove the lawful acquisition of “significant amounts,” meaning crypto holdings worth over 100,000 euros (about $109,300), during the holding period.

title: Binance Fully Lifts Withdrawal Suspension a Month After $6.3 Billion Hack
summary:
Bitcoin Magazine

Binance Fully Lifts Withdrawal Suspension a Month After $6.3 Billion Hack
Binance said its withdrawal recovery work is complete and the suspension tied to the Oct. 29 hack has been fully lifted, as researchers track North Korean launderers moving the stolen funds.
This post Binance...
content:
Binance has fully lifted the withdrawal suspension it put in place after last month’s record $6.3 billion hack, saying its recovery work is complete and that withdrawals are open across nearly all networks.

“Our withdrawal recovery work is completed and the withdrawal suspension from the security incident has been fully lifted,” the exchange said in an X post Thursday afternoon. A small number of networks remain paused for maintenance, which Binance called standard practice and said was unrelated to the hack.

The update closes out a month of phased reopenings. Binance confirmed the breach on Oct. 29, saying its initial investigation pointed to a compromised DevOps engineer’s laptop that gave the attacker access to a service container, which was then used to submit unauthorized withdrawals.

The world’s largest crypto exchange stopped all customer withdrawals for two days after the theft, Reuters reported. When they first reopened, customers pulled a net $4.7 billion off the platform, Binance said on Nov. 2.

Binance covered the losses

Binance said on Nov. 12 that it had completed coverage of the affected assets with more than $6.34 billion of company funds. The money came from a partial draw on its Secure Asset Fund for Users, part of its futures insurance fund and its corporate treasury, and the exchange pledged to rebuild SAFU to about $1 billion.

Coverage is not the same as recovery. Binance replaced the stolen tokens from its own books, while about $2.85 billion of the stolen funds have been frozen remotely by the companies that issue them. The rest remains in the hands of the attackers.

U.S. authorities have blamed North Korean hackers for the theft, which North Korea denies. On Nov. 23, the Justice Department moved to forfeit more than $1.1 billion in USDC that Circle froze, and said the U.S. has helped freeze, seize or return more than $2.9 billion since the attack.

Launderers turn to THORChain and coinjoin

The unfrozen funds are on the move. North Korean launderers have stepped up transfers through THORChain and a coinjoin service in recent days, blockchain researchers told Reuters, as part of an operation spanning tens of thousands of transactions across blockchains.

Chainalysis and Elliptic estimate that more than $600 million of the stolen crypto has passed through THORChain, though Elliptic said that figure could count funds that went through more than once. TRM Labs estimates THORChain earned as much as $1 million in fees from the swaps.

Separately, $342 million has moved through a coinjoin service mostly coordinated by a pseudonymous figure named Kruw, Elliptic said. A coinjoin combines coins from many users into a single transaction, so their origin is no longer visible on the blockchain. Elliptic has said the launderers will still need other services, such as over-the-counter brokers, to turn the coins into cash.

The FBI on Oct. 31 published wallet addresses used by the attacker and asked crypto service providers, including the network of computers that runs THORChain, to block them. In a video posted Thursday, THORChain co-founder Chad Barraford said 98% of trading on the network was for people’s “own individual financial freedom and liberty.”

THORChain, which describes itself as decentralized, says on its website that it does not “censor” transactions or run Know-Your-Customer checks. Ari Redbord, global head of policy at TRM Labs, called the FBI’s move to single out the network’s operators “pretty extraordinary.”

Redbord said the laundering could take months or even years, and that cashing out even a fraction would be a windfall for North Korea. The total stolen from Binance equals about a sixth of the country’s estimated gross domestic product.

“They don’t have to get a lot off in order to make this all worthwhile for them,” Redbord said.

Micah Zimmerman

Micah first discovered Bitcoin in 2018 but remained a skeptic on the sidelines for too long. Since 2021, he has covered crypto and business and now works as a news reporter for Bitcoin Magazine, based in North Carolina.

title: China sets March 2027 rollout for blockchain identity regulations
summary: China has issued new regulations governing blockchain-based digital identities, setting rules for cross-platform verification and data privacy.
content:
Latest NewsPublishedNov 27, 2026

China has issued new regulations governing blockchain-based digital identities, setting rules for cross-platform verification and data privacy.

China published new regulations on blockchain-based digital identities on Nov. 27, establishing a framework for identity verification and interoperability across government institutions and private-sector platforms.

The regulations, which will take effect on March 1, 2027, were jointly issued by 11 government departments, including the People’s Bank of China and the Cyberspace Administration of China.

Under the rules, China’s national blockchain network will provide the infrastructure for a digital identity system operated by entities authorized by the country’s cyberspace regulator, in cooperation with identity authentication and credential providers.

Digital identities powered by blockchain technology can allow users to verify their identity or credentials across platforms without disclosing unnecessary personal information.

According to Chinese state-backed media outlet China Net, the identity chain will bring together multiple institutions “to achieve multi-party consensus through blockchain technology.”

The regulations are part of China’s broader push to expand blockchain adoption, with the country targeting 2030 to largely complete its national blockchain infrastructure while maintaining restrictions on cryptocurrency-related activities in mainland China.

Limits on digital identity data collection

Individuals and organizations will be able to voluntarily register digital identities and use verifiable credentials to disclose specific information, such as educational or professional qualifications, without necessarily revealing all the associated data.

Platforms and digital identity service providers will be required to follow data minimization requirements, collecting only the information necessary for identity verification. They will be prohibited from using that data for cross-platform profiling or targeted advertising.

The regulations aim to address barriers to identity verification across regions, industries and platforms. They also encourage interoperability with digital yuan and the adoption of distributed digital identities in sectors including finance, taxation, transportation and customs.

Friday, 27/11/2026 | 17:25 GMT by Tanya Chepkova

  • Starting November 28, Vantage’s 1:1000 gold leverage will apply to positions up to 100 oz outside news periods.
  • The upgrade coincides with Seychelles broker RADEX launching 1:5000 dynamic FX leverage.

Offshore Forex and CFD broker Vantage Markets raised the maximum leverage for small positions on 24/7 gold CFD to 1:1000. This is the second increase since the contract launch in July 2026.

According to the company, the change will enhance the client trading experience and strengthen product competitiveness, as offshore brokers increasingly use high leverage to attract and stimulate trading on small retail accounts.

Big leverage for Small positions

Starting from November 28, the maximum leverage for XAUUSD247 - gold CFD trading seven days a week - will be raised from 1:500 to 1:1000.

Vantage Markets leverage tiers are based on the size of the leveraged position. The new conditions will be available outside news periods for the smallest lots up to 100 oz.

Other tiers will also be upgraded. Thus, 100-300 oz positions can be traded with a maximum leverage of 1:500, while the largest lots from 9,000 oz and higher will be traded with 1:1 leverage.

Vantage Markets is an offshore brand operated by VIG Group, a full-service investment dealer authorised and regulated by the Mauritius Financial Services Commission (FSC).

The company explicitly states that it does not target or provide services to clients in the US, Canada, China, Hong Kong, Singapore, sanctioned countries, or countries on FATF lists.

From 1:100 to 1:1000 in Four Months

Vantage Markets launched XAUUSD247 in July 2026 to meet customers' demand for round-the-clock gold trading. The contract runs seven days a week, subject to scheduled maintenance and regional availability.

At launch, the company announced 1:100 leverage for positions from 1 to 100 oz, with no separate commission. In September, the CFD broker raised the maximum leverage to 1:500 and expanded its availability for a wider range of positions in October.

In November, the maximum leverage rose to 1:1000, ten times the initial level.

To protect traders' capital, the account specifications say, "leverage for new positions may be dynamically adjusted during designated high-risk windows, such as weekend market closures".

IC, FXGT and Born2Trade also offer extreme leverage under strict conditions, for limited asset classes, restricted position sizes and trading conditions.

IC, FXGT and Born2Trade also offer extreme leverage under strict conditions, for limited asset classes, restricted position sizes and trading conditions.

Offshore brokers are using four- and five-digit leverage ratios to compete for small-balance retail flow in high-velocity assets like gold and FX. Yet the fine print shows that dealing desks are keeping a tight leash on their own balance-sheet exposure.
