Russia’s VTB Opens Bitcoin Trading as Central Bank Finalizes Crypto Test
VTB began letting qualified investors trade bitcoin in its app on Friday, a day after the Bank of Russia approved the knowledge test every crypto buyer must pass. SPB Exchange plans to open spot trading Dec. 1...
content:
Russian bank VTB began letting brokerage clients buy and sell bitcoin in its investing app on Friday, a day after the Bank of Russia approved the knowledge test every Russian crypto buyer now has to pass.

Starting Nov. 27, clients of VTB’s brokerage can trade cryptocurrencies in the VTB My Investments app, the broker said. For now, the trades happen over the counter rather than on an exchange, and access is limited to qualified investors, the legal term for Russians who meet wealth or experience thresholds, who also pass the new test.

“In our model, access to cryptocurrencies will require qualified investor status and passing special testing,” Andrei Yatskov, head of brokerage services at VTB, said. He said the test would appear in the app on Nov. 27 and work like the bank’s existing tests for other instruments.

VTB handles the buying, storage and record-keeping itself on Russian infrastructure. To trade, clients need to open a separate digital account at VTB’s digital depository, where the crypto is held, on top of their regular brokerage account. The bank received its digital depository and crypto exchange licenses on Oct. 6.

“At the start, we will focus on buying and selling cryptocurrencies, and then we will introduce additional services as regulation develops,” Yatskov said.

Eight questions before the first trade

The launch came quickly after the regulator moved. On Nov. 26, the Bank of Russia approved the first basic standards for brokers and crypto exchange offices, setting the rules for the test. Every investor has to take it, qualified or not, and it is free.

Buyers must answer at least seven of eight questions correctly. The standard lays out eight topic blocks, from regulation, technical basics and information security to stablecoins, low-liquidity coins, address labeling and blocked transactions, and volatility, with one question drawn at random from each.

Investors who fail can try once more the same day, with different questions. Brokers are barred from sharing the correct answers with clients or telling them which questions they missed. A passing result stays valid for one year from the test date or the latest trade, whichever comes later.

The test was the missing piece for Russian banks. When retail buying became legal on Nov. 17, T-Bank said it was waiting on a market standard for testing, and VTB said it was waiting on the remaining rules. Under the broker standard, the industry’s self-regulatory organization has three working days after publication to send brokers the answer options and correct answers.

Ordinary investors still face tight limits once they pass. Non-qualified buyers can only purchase bitcoin, ether and Tether’s USDT, and no more than 300,000 rubles a year through a single intermediary.

SPB Exchange sets Dec. 1 start

Exchange trading is next. SPB Exchange said Friday it will open spot trading in bitcoin, ether and USDT against the ruble on Dec. 1, after the Bank of Russia added it to the registry of digital depositories on Nov. 27. Trading will run from 9 a.m. to 4 p.m. Moscow time, with same-day settlement in rubles.

Investors won’t all get in on day one. SPB Exchange said brokers will first use the market to set up their systems, and access will open as each broker is ready. TRX and USDC are also approved, but only for qualified investors, with a start date still to come.

Russian exchanges have been allowed to run organized crypto trading since Nov. 22, once the central bank signs off on their rules. Moscow Exchange has also been aiming to open bitcoin trading on Dec. 1.

“We expect that in 2027, as brokers become ready, investor access to the spot market will expand and new products and investment services will appear,” said Evgeny Serdyukov, SPB Exchange’s chief executive.

Micah Zimmerman

Micah first discovered Bitcoin in 2018 but remained a skeptic on the sidelines for too long. Since 2021, he has covered crypto and business and now works as a news reporter for Bitcoin Magazine, based in North Carolina.

title: Bitcoin price drops below $59K as Anthropic joins tech stock rebound
summary: Bitcoin price volatility returned at the Wall Street open as BTC/USD dropped to local lows of $58,700 while stocks and gold headed higher.
content:
Bitcoin touched $62,100 on Friday as risk assets and precious metals rose during a shortened US trading session following the Thanksgiving holiday.

Key points:

  • Bitcoin (BTC) experienced sudden volatility at Friday’s Wall Street open as sellers erased a move above $62,000.
  • Crypto positions worth $228 million were liquidated in the hour ending at 3:00 p.m. UTC.
  • Gold sought to cement its rebound after falling sharply below its 200-day moving average of $4,373 per ounce.

BTC price suddenly drops to $58,700

Data from TradingView showed BTC/USD gaining up to 2.7% as US stock futures rose ahead of the Wall Street open. The pair then fell bellow $59,000 as sellers returned to the market following Thursday’s Thanksgiving closure of US stock markets.

BTC/USD one-hour chart. Source: Cointelegraph/TradingView

Data from CoinGlass showed that $228 million in crypto positions were liquidated in the hour ending at 3:00 p.m. UTC.

BTC/USD vs. crypto liquidations. Source: CoinGlass

Traders appeared eager to increase tech-stock exposure during Friday’s shortened US trading session, with the closing bell due at 1:00 p.m. Eastern time. The S&P 500 and tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite Index opened up 0.9% and 1.4%, respectively.

Tech stocks showed mixed performance, with Anthropic (Nasdaq: ANT) gaining 4% to trade above $87. The stock was about 18% higher than Wednesday’s low of $73.90.

Anthropic stock one-hour chart. Source: Cointelegraph/TradingView

At the same time, Nvidia shares fell 1.5% to $147 after the open.

“The hyperscalers ultimately have to get an ROI, and they ultimately need to rebuild their free cash flow, and people like Anthropic need to prove that they can generate the revenue growth that people expect and ultimately be very profitable and free-cash-flow generative as well,” Richard Clode, a portfolio manager at Janus Henderson, told CNBC.

Precious metals also rallied, with silver rising as much as 7.4% on the day, while gold (XAU/USD) was 2% higher at $3,635 per ounce as of 3 p.m. UTC.

XAU/USD one-day chart with the 200-day SMA. Source: Cointelegraph/TradingView

On Wednesday, trading resource The Kobeissi Letter flagged highly oversold conditions in gold, which traded 20% below its 200-day simple moving average (SMA), currently at $4,373.

“This comes as gold prices have dropped -37% from their January intraday peak, their largest drawdown within a 12-month period since the early 1980s,” it wrote on X, calling gold’s 2026 retracement “one of its most severe declines in history.”

Analysis: Bitcoin “closer to seller capitulation”

Bitcoin price action diverged from stocks and precious metals as traders sold into the modest post-holiday gains.

Related: Crypto on notice as hawkish Fed risks December ‘meltdown’

Crypto trader and analyst Rekt Capital highlighted the intensity of the ongoing selling pressure on Bitcoin. “Since Bitcoin experienced a breakout on seller volume, Bitcoin’s price tumbled -27% to the downside,” the analyst wrote.

“Bitcoin has since also suffered 4 consecutive weeks of above-average sell-side volume, getting Bitcoin closer to seller capitulation & exhaustion.”

BTC/USD one-week chart. Source: Cointelegraph/TradingView

Previously, Cointelegraph reported that a growing share of the BTC supply was held at an unrealized loss as capitulation signals reappeared.

title: Bitcoin Whales Accumulate $7.4 Billion in BTC, Breaking a Nine Year Pattern
summary: Key takeaways Balances in Bitcoin addresses holding 1,000 to 10,000 BTC rose by 121,117 BTC from September 30 to November 21, worth about $7.4 billion at a reference price of $61,000. Bitcoin fell 29.5% over the same period. This group reduced its holdings in seven of the previous nine fourth quarte...
content:
Key takeaways

  • Balances in Bitcoin addresses holding 1,000 to 10,000 BTC rose by 121,117 BTC from September 30 to November 21, worth about $7.4 billion at a reference price of $61,000. Bitcoin fell 29.5% over the same period.
  • This group reduced its holdings in seven of the previous nine fourth quarters. Its 4.29% increase so far in Q4 2026 is the largest fourth-quarter gain since 2020.
  • The group’s unrealized profit margin dropped from 33.9% to 5.7% by November 21, the lowest reading of 2026 in the report.
  • Addresses holding at least 1,000 BTC recorded $2.1 billion in net realized losses through November 21. Exchange inflows from transaction outputs of at least 1,000 BTC also picked up in November.
  • Rising address balances alone cannot establish how much new money entered Bitcoin or whether its price has bottomed.

Bitcoin whales have reversed their usual year-end pattern. Between September 30 and November 21, balances in addresses holding 1,000 to 10,000 BTC rose by 121,117 BTC even though Bitcoin lost 29.5% of its value. At a reference price of $61,000, those additional coins are worth roughly $7.4 billion.

The figures come from CryptoQuant’s November 27 research report, which was supported by crypto lender CoinRabbit. The study excludes exchange and mining-pool addresses from its balance cohorts. Its findings are a snapshot through November 21, not a final tally for the quarter.

The timing matters. NewsBTC recently reported more than $2 billion in US spot Bitcoin ETF outflows. Fund withdrawals and rising whale balances point in different directions, but they measure different things. Neither tells us whether the same investors are moving their money from ETFs into direct Bitcoin ownership.

A broader measure from Maketo’s whale holdings data puts the balance of addresses with at least 1,000 BTC at 7.22 million BTC on November 26, up 54,379 BTC over the preceding 30 days. That group includes exchange and custody addresses, so it provides a separate view of where coins are held rather than an independent check of CryptoQuant’s 121,117 BTC figure.

Bitcoin Whales Reverse Their Year-End Balance Trend

The combined balance of the 1,000 to 10,000 BTC cohort at just under 2.95 million BTC on November 21, up from 2.83 million at the end of September.

Large addresses reduced their balances in seven of the nine preceding fourth quarters. Only 2019 and 2020 escaped that pattern. The 4.29% increase recorded so far this quarter is the largest Q4 gain since 2020, although December could still change the result.

For comparison, the cohort lost nearly 203,000 BTC over Q4 2025. This year’s increase has come during a falling market, rather than a rally.

There is a catch in calling this a $7.4 billion accumulation. The figure values the additional coins at a reference price; it does not measure the dollars spent buying them. Transfers between addresses, including movements across the cohort’s balance thresholds, can change the total without a market purchase.

The increase tells us where Bitcoin is sitting. It does not tell us how much fresh capital is behind it. That distinction matters when liquidity is scarce.

Bitcoin Whales Are Running Out Of Profits To Protect

The 121,117 BTC figure makes for a bullish headline. The number I would pay closer attention to is the remaining profit margin.

Among addresses holding between 1,000 and 10,000 BTC, the unrealized profit margin fell from 33.9% at the end of September to 5.7% on November 21, its lowest reading of 2026 in the report.

The deterioration is even clearer in dollar terms. Combined unrealized profits for addresses holding at least 1,000 BTC stood at about $24 billion on November 21, down from a peak of $294 billion in August 2025.

Across the broader group of addresses holding at least 1,000 BTC, net realized losses reached approximately $2.1 billion in the first 52 days of Q4. The on-chain data suggests that some large holders are already moving coins at a loss rather than waiting for a recovery.

The relevant distinction is between the balance held at a given date and the profit or loss on coins that move. A growing balance does not prevent other coins within the cohort from being spent below their estimated cost basis.

Exchange deposits deserve a closer look, too. Inflows from unspent transaction outputs (UTXOs) of at least 1,000 BTC averaged 5,012 BTC per day in November through the report’s cutoff, compared with 3,239 in October. That is a measure of large coin outputs, not a count of individual whales.

November’s pickup should not obscure the bigger picture: the quarter-to-date average of 3,955 BTC per day remained below the 2019–2025 Q4 average of 4,575 BTC. Large deposits are not proof of sales, and a rise in this metric alone does not establish that selling pressure has intensified.

What Would Confirm A Bitcoin Market Bottom?

The 2018 and 2022 bear markets offer a useful comparison, though not a roadmap for this one.

Balances in the 1,000 to 10,000 BTC cohort declined in both of those fourth quarters. Their average unrealized profit margins were negative, while the group still had a positive margin at the November 21 reading this year.

Today’s accumulation may be a sign that some large holders are willing to retain exposure through the downturn. The address data cannot establish their motives or identify how much of the increase came from new purchases.

I would not call a market bottom on these numbers alone.

A further price decline could wipe out the cohort’s remaining profit cushion. Whether that produces more selling depends on the holders’ liquidity needs and positioning, neither of which can be read directly from address balances.

The next test is whether large-address balances keep rising while net realized losses and large exchange deposits ease. That combination, alongside evidence of renewed spot demand, would make the recovery case more convincing.

For now, the change in year-end positioning is real within CryptoQuant’s measured cohort. Evidence of a durable recovery is still missing.

title: New York Wins $1.37 Billion Judgment Against NovaTech Crypto Ponzi Founders
summary:
Bitcoin Magazine

New York Wins $1.37 Billion Judgment Against NovaTech Crypto Ponzi Founders
A New York judge ordered NovaTech founders Cynthia and Eddy Petion to pay more than $1.37 billion over a crypto Ponzi scheme that targeted Haitian communities.
This post New York Wins $1.37 Billion Judgment...
content:
A New York judge has ordered the founders of NovaTech, a cryptocurrency investment scheme that targeted Haitian communities, to pay more than $1.37 billion, closing out the state’s case against a couple who fled the country rather than answer it.

Justice Anar Rathod Patel of the New York County Supreme Court signed the order on Nov. 24. It holds Cynthia and Eddy Petion and their companies NovaTech Ltd, NovaTech Advisors and NovaPay jointly liable for $1,367,023,585 in disgorgement and interest.

New York Attorney General Letitia James announced the win on Wednesday.

“Today’s historic judgment finally delivers some semblance of justice for the thousands of New Yorkers who were targeted by this merciless scam,” James said. “NovaTech cruelly targeted immigrant families through faith and community groups with the promise of a better life while robbing them of their life savings.”

Where the $1.37 billion figure comes from

The award matches what the attorney general’s office asked for in October. The figure starts with the cryptocurrency investors sent to NovaTech’s wallet at payment processor CoinPayments, which totaled about $1.16 billion from August 2019 through May 2023, according to an affirmation filed by the state.

Prosecutors subtracted the roughly $26 million NovaTech actually moved to its trading platform, leaving $1.13 billion in principal. Nine percent annual interest from June 2023 through September 2025 added another $232.5 million.

NovaTech’s traders lost about $18.2 million of the money they did trade, the filing said. Everything else paid out of the wallet, including so-called returns and recruitment bonuses, came from other investors’ deposits.

Cynthia Petion was the only authorized user on the CoinPayments account, and the state says she approved at least $134.5 million in crypto withdrawals to wallets belonging to her and her husband.

The judge also ordered the Petions’ earlier venture, AWS Mining, to pay about $1.46 million. Cynthia Petion owes a separate $4.69 million tied to her promotion of that scheme.

A NovaTech scheme built on prayer groups

AWS Mining sold crypto mining contracts and promised 15% to 20% monthly returns before it collapsed in 2019, according to the attorney general’s office. The Petions then launched NovaTech, falsely marketed it as a registered hedge fund broker and advertised trading profits of about 2% to 4% a week.

Promoters recruited through prayer groups, WhatsApp chats and ads in Haitian Creole. More than 11,000 New Yorkers invested, alongside what the state called hundreds of thousands of investors worldwide.

NovaTech collapsed in May 2023, and tens of thousands of investors couldn’t withdraw their crypto. The state sued in June 2024.

The Petions never answered the complaint. The court entered a default judgment in August 2025 that found they violated New York’s Martin Act and banned them from the securities, commodities and cryptocurrency industries. They also never produced the investor accounting the court ordered.

Because the money award also came by default, NovaTech’s founders never contested the figures. The order lets the state docket it as a money judgment and begin collection, though it’s unclear how much can be recovered from defendants who left the U.S.

Four of NovaTech’s top promoters settled in October. Martin Zizi, Frantz Ciceron, Ricardo Roy Sr. and James Corbett agreed to pay nearly $6 million combined for the benefit of victims and accepted permanent industry bans.

The judgment lands as regulators step up crypto fraud cases. Last week, the SEC froze assets in a separate $560 million crypto trading Ponzi scheme run out of Indianapolis, weeks after it charged companies in a $130 million crypto case.

“My office will always fight to bring fraudsters who take advantage of hardworking New Yorkers to justice,” James said.

Micah Zimmerman

Micah first discovered Bitcoin in 2018 but remained a skeptic on the sidelines for too long. Since 2021, he has covered crypto and business and now works as a news reporter for Bitcoin Magazine, based in North Carolina.

title: BingX Lets CFD Traders Split Strategies Across Three Accounts
summary:
BingX now supports multiple CFD standard accounts, allowing eligible users to create up to three separate accounts and use them for different trading strategies. 
By default, one main CFD account can have up to three sub-accounts, each with its own funds, margin, positions and orders, providing trad...
content:
2026-11-27T17:30:00.000+02:00

Friday, 27/11/2026 | 15:30 GMT by Tanya Chepkova

  • Each account has separate funds, margin and positions, with transfers supported between them.
  • Maximum leverage reaches 2,000:1, but actual availability depends on trading rules.

BingX now supports multiple CFD standard accounts, allowing eligible users to create up to three separate accounts and use them for different trading strategies.

By default, one main CFD account can have up to three sub-accounts, each with its own funds, margin, positions and orders, providing traders with more flexibility to manage risk and monitor strategy performance.

How the New Structure Works

The update applies to BingX’s existing CFD offering, which covers precious metals, stock indices, foreign exchange and commodities. These contracts allow customers to trade price movements without owning the underlying assets.

Each standard account gets its own separate MetaTrader 5 ID. The accounts can be used to monitor the capital and performance of different strategies in isolation, with the combined equity and unrealised Pnl of all the strategies visible on the platform’s Assets page.

Users can also transfer funds between their CFD accounts and switch the account they're trading on. BingX says this is an addition of account management functionality rather than a new CFD account type.

Leverage and Pricing Set by Account

New accounts default to what BingX refers to as "zero-fee mode". Other pricing options (including an ultra-low spread mode) are subject to user eligibility. When opening an account, users can select maximum leverage of 500:1, 1,000:1 or 2,000:1. The default is 500:1, and the selected maximum cannot be changed after creation.

Actual trading leverage depends on the instrument, account and applicable trading rules. Existing accounts will retain their MT5 ID, balance, positions, leverage and server details.

The number of additional accounts you can have is dictated by the limit that's shown on the platform. Although BingX announced the feature on 27 November, its support guide lists the web launch as 19 November.

BingX Catches up with Competitors

Multiple trading accounts are already available at CFD brokers. Pepperstone, for example, lets clients open several accounts under one profile. Pepperstone Crypto exchange also offers ways to separate strategies.

Bybit’s standard subaccounts have independent balances and performance tracking, with optional separate logins and API access. However, that functionality does not extend to its CFD offering.

The update brings BingX’s MT5 offering closer to the account-management model used by traditional CFD brokers. For users trading both crypto and CFDs on the platform, it adds a way to separate CFD strategies, funds and margin without opening additional user profiles.

title: Spain Lets Anti-Money Laundering Unit Freeze Crypto Accounts Without a Judge
summary:
Bitcoin Magazine
Spain Lets Anti-Money Laundering Unit Freeze Crypto Accounts Without a Judge
A royal decree lets Sepblac, Spain's financial intelligence unit, freeze crypto, bank and payment accounts for up to five business days without a court order.
This post Spain Lets Anti-Money Laundering Unit...
content:
Spain has given its financial intelligence unit the power to freeze crypto accounts on its own authority, without first getting a judge’s approval, when it suspects money laundering or terrorist financing.

The change was published in Spain’s official state gazette on Wednesday as part of Royal Decree-Law 44/2026, a sweeping decree that mostly deals with consumer credit contracts and the sale of bad loan portfolios. Its sixth final provision adds a new Article 46 bis to the country’s 2010 anti-money laundering law.

The new article lets the Executive Service of the Commission for the Prevention of Money Laundering and Monetary Offenses, known as Sepblac, suspend or refuse to authorize a transaction in progress. It can also suspend the use of a bank, payment or crypto-asset account, or a business relationship, when there are “indications” that it could be tied to money laundering or terrorist financing.

According to the text, the goal is to preserve the funds while Sepblac carries out its analysis and checks whether the suspicion holds up. If it does, the unit passes the information to the competent authorities so they can take further action.

Five days for accounts, 10 for transactions

The decree sets two separate time limits. Sepblac can hold a pending transaction for no more than 10 business days, and it can freeze an account or business relationship for no more than five. Either hold must be lifted sooner if it is no longer needed to preserve the funds.

When the suspicion comes from a suspicious activity report filed by a bank or other regulated firm, Sepblac must issue the suspension within three business days of that report. When the case comes from the unit’s own analysis, the decree says it must act “as soon as possible.”

Once those deadlines pass, the freeze ends unless a court ratifies or extends it at the request of the public prosecutor’s office. Appeals against a court’s decision follow Spain’s criminal procedure law.

The decree also shields Sepblac, its staff and the firms that carry out its orders from liability. Firms that ignore a suspension order commit an offense under the anti-money laundering law. Sepblac can also act at the request of Spanish police and security forces, or of financial intelligence units in other EU states and outside the bloc.

Why Spain made the change

Until now, Sepblac could only use this power when a foreign financial intelligence unit asked it to. The government said in the decree’s preamble that the limit is a deficiency the Financial Action Task Force will assess, and that waiting longer could hurt Spain’s international evaluation.

The government also said the speed of financial transactions, especially online, lets possibly criminal funds move before authorities can finish their analysis. The provision transposes Article 24 of an EU directive adopted in May 2024 on the mechanisms member states must set up to fight money laundering.

The rule takes effect Jan. 25, 2027, two months after the decree’s publication. As a royal decree-law, it must also be put to a vote in Spain’s Congress of Deputies within 30 days to be validated or repealed.

The decree does not name individual crypto platforms, and it is not yet clear how exchanges operating in Spain will receive and carry out the orders. Several European governments have been moving the same way. Poland’s parliament voted 240-202 this month to let officials freeze bitcoin and bank funds of people on a national sanctions list before a court reviews the case.

Other moves in Europe have gone the opposite way. France’s Senate rejected amendments that would have forced holders to declare self-custody wallets worth €100,000 or more, while Binance is closing accounts in four EU countries at the end of the year.

Under the decree, crypto-asset accounts fall under the same five-day freeze limit as bank and payment accounts.

Micah Zimmerman

Micah first discovered Bitcoin in 2018 but remained a skeptic on the sidelines for too long. Since 2021, he has covered crypto and business and now works as a news reporter for Bitcoin Magazine, based in North Carolina.

title: What was Coinbase worth while Nasdaq was closed?
summary: A Thanksgiving buyer paid 106.24 USDC per Coinbase share. Whether that looked like a holiday rally depended on when you’d last checked the stock.
content:
Tokenized stocks give investors another place to trade after the closing bell. Coinbase’s Thanksgiving tape shows why it still matters where else the shares changed hands and how many you want to trade.

On Thanksgiving afternoon, a buyer spent 125.49 USDC (USDC) on tokenized Coinbase shares while Nasdaq was closed. If you’d last checked the stock at Wednesday’s closing bell, that small purchase seemed to carry news of a holiday rally.

Coinbase had closed at $103.72, and the buyer on OKXICE paid 106.24 USDC per token, an apparent gain of 2.4%. But if you’d stayed for Wednesday’s after-hours session, you’d have seen the shares reach $106.91, according to brokerage Public.

From there, the very same token trade looked about 0.6% lower, valuing USDC at a dollar. However, the choice of where to start measuring was enough to turn a gain into a decline.

Related: Nasdaq exec pushes for common EU rules on tokenized securities

An investor in Germany had an even fresher price to go on. Early on Thanksgiving, 142 Coinbase shares changed hands on Tradegate at 97.50 euros apiece, roughly $107 at that day’s exchange rate.

What changed for the afternoon buyer was that they could open a wallet and buy Coinbase exposure over the holiday, and anyone following the stock could see exactly what that order cost.

Finding oneself on the other side of that trade with $10,000 worth of Coinbase to sell, the blockchain could tell you to four decimal places what someone had paid for just over one token, but could you get that price for 94?

title: Bitcoin Price Trades Near $61,300 as Tech Stock Futures Rally
summary:
Bitcoin Magazine

Bitcoin Price Trades Near $61,300 as Tech Stock Futures Rally
The bitcoin price traded near $61,300 on Friday as tech stock futures jumped ahead of a shortened Wall Street session, putting bitcoin on track to snap a seven-week losing streak.
This post Bitcoin Price Trades Near $61,...
content:
The bitcoin price traded near $61,300 on Friday morning, as tech stock futures jumped ahead of a holiday-shortened session on Wall Street. Bitcoin price is on track for its first weekly gain after seven straight weekly losses, though it is still down about 20% in November.

The bitcoin price was up about 1.7% early Friday and set to add 4.8% for the week, Investing.com reported, extending a recovery from a two-year low of $57,325.70 hit earlier in the week. Bitcoin slumped below $57,500 on Wednesday as the Nasdaq sank at the open, before a late rebound in tech shares lifted risk assets.

Short sellers helped fuel the bounce. Shorts made up 77% of $84.7 million in bitcoin liquidations over the past day, while futures open interest was little changed. That suggests forced short covering, rather than fresh leverage, supplied much of the lift.

Tech futures lead the risk rebound

Nasdaq 100 futures rose 2.2% by 6:42 a.m. ET, Reuters reported, as investors returned from Thanksgiving and piled back into battered AI-linked shares. Nvidia gained 3.6% in premarket trading, while AMD climbed 4.4% and Broadcom added 3.4%. S&P 500 futures rose 1.6%, and Dow futures gained 1.3%.

“There have been some signs that the tech selloff has stabilised for now, and that risk appetite is returning to markets,” Deutsche Bank analysts said in a note cited by Reuters. The S&P 500 is headed for its best week since April, though it remains on course for its worst November since 2008.

Bitcoin price has followed that rebound but lagged it. The major U.S. stock indexes are each up around 4% on the week, and silver jumped about 7% to above $44 an ounce on Friday while gold added 2.5% to above $3,670. Stocks close early at 1 p.m. ET, and the bond market shuts at 2 p.m.

Rate hike bets and ETF outflows linger

The macro backdrop still weighs on the bitcoin price. Traders are almost fully pricing in a Federal Reserve rate hike in December after data this week showed the economy grew faster than first estimated in the third quarter and inflation accelerated in October, Reuters reported. Third-quarter GDP growth was revised up to 4.3%, and the 10-year Treasury yield slipped to 4.84%.

Spot bitcoin ETFs are also still losing cash. The U.S. funds lost $453 million on Wednesday, their seventh straight day of outflows, with BlackRock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust accounting for $329.7 million. That pushed November outflows to about $5.39 billion, extending what was already a record month for the funds.

Crypto stocks and miners in focus

Crypto stocks face their own test in Friday’s short session. Strategy shares rose 3.1% to $79.96 on Wednesday, while Coinbase gained 1.3% to $103.72. Bitcoin miners that have moved into AI hosting tracked the tech rally, with IREN and Cipher Digital each gaining 8% in premarket trading.

Mining economics remain tight with the bitcoin price this low. CleanSpark has weighed selling more bitcoin than it mines after a $987 million loss, and network mining difficulty jumped 7.61% early Friday, reversing most of a 9.13% drop on Nov. 14. That means miners must spend more computing power for each bitcoin they earn.

In options markets, about $7 billion of bitcoin contracts expired at 3 a.m. ET Friday, with traders positioned defensively going into the expiry. Over the past day, four of the six busiest bitcoin options were calls, three of them at $62,000 to $64,000 strikes, though the single busiest contract was a Dec. 25 put at $50,000.

At the time of writing, the bitcoin price is near $61,300.

Micah first discovered Bitcoin in 2018 but remained a skeptic on the sidelines for too long. Since 2021, he has covered crypto and business and now works as a news reporter for Bitcoin Magazine, based in North Carolina.

title: Binance to launch tokenized IPO program after regulatory approval: Yi He
summary: Binance is hiring for equity capital markets roles, including an analyst to develop tokenized equity products and assess prospective issuers.
content:
Latest NewsPublishedNov 27, 2026

Binance is hiring for equity capital markets roles, including an analyst to develop tokenized equity products and assess prospective issuers.

Cryptocurrency exchange Binance plans to launch a tokenized initial public offering (IPO) program for onchain share issuance once it receives regulatory approval.

The project forms part of Binance’s real-world asset strategy and will involve collaboration with decentralized finance projects, Binance co-founder and co-CEO Yi He said during BNB Demo Night in Bangkok on Friday.

“Actually, that’s a professional IPO process,” He said, distinguishing the planned program from simply listing new assets on the exchange.

Her comments follow Binance’s recent job postings for equity capital markets roles, which fueled speculation about the exchange’s plans to facilitate onchain IPOs.

One job posting seeks an equity capital markets research analyst to help develop tokenized equity products, evaluate prospective issuers and assess deal structures, pricing and allocation. The role requires at least four years of relevant experience and an understanding of traditional IPOs and follow-on offerings.

Cointelegraph reached out to Binance for further details but had not received a response by publication.

title: Bigger Client Accounts Bring 40% Less Revenue at One Online Broker
summary:
Clients of Tiger Brokers hold more money per head than clients of its larger rival Futu. They bring in about 40% less revenue per client, FM Intelligence analysis published today (Friday) shows.
The comparison, part of FM Intelligence's Featured Broker analysis of Tiger Brokers, divides each company...
content:
2026-11-27T15:39:00.000+02:00

Friday, 27/11/2026 | 13:39 GMT by Damian Chmiel

  • Its clients hold more money on average, but that money trades less often.
  • A larger margin book has not closed the gap, and new Hong Kong signups deposit below the existing average.

Clients of Tiger Brokers hold more money per head than clients of its larger rival Futu. They bring in about 40% less revenue per client, FM Intelligence analysis published today (Friday) shows.

The comparison, part of FM Intelligence's Featured Broker analysis of Tiger Brokers, divides each company's third-quarter revenue and client assets by its funded clients.

It cuts against a common reading of broker results, in which record client assets point to record revenue. UP Fintech, Tiger's Nasdaq-listed parent, reported record client assets for the third quarter on Tuesday, while revenue per client stayed well below Futu's.

Where the Revenue Gap Comes From

FM Intelligence split the gap by source. Most of it sits in two lines of the income statement, commissions and interest, with other revenue making up a small remainder.

On commissions, the difference lies mainly in how often client money trades. Each dollar held at Futu changes hands more often, even after its third-quarter trading volume fell from the previous quarter.

Price may explain part of the rest, but the two companies report their commission rates on different bases.

Interest is the less obvious half. Tiger lends more against its client assets than Futu does, yet earns less interest per client. Futu holds a larger share of client money as cash, which can earn interest for a broker without any lending.

Client balances drive the same line at bigger brokers. At Interactive Brokers, net interest income rose in the third quarter as balances grew and yields fell.

What the New Clients Bring

Most of Tiger's new clients in the quarter came from Singapore and Hong Kong, management said on the earnings call. Its mainland Chinese base is shrinking after UP Fintech disclosed fines and confiscated income from China's securities regulator in May.

Whether the newcomers change the picture depends on how they trade and borrow more than on how much they deposit. New Hong Kong clients brought in less money on average than the existing base holds, according to management figures cited in the analysis.

Futu faces a different pressure. Its revenue per client has fallen over the past year as it adds overseas accounts that hold less on average, in pursuit of the new-client target it set for 2026. The gap between the two brokers has narrowed over the year.

The arithmetic reaches beyond the two firms. A CFD or multi-asset broker adding stock trading for existing clients can grow deposits without growing revenue per dollar held, unless turnover or interest-bearing cash rises with them.

The comparison covers two brokers, so it gives a benchmark rather than an industry norm.

The full FM Intelligence analysis measures what each dollar of client assets earns at both brokers, splits the gap by revenue source and sets a scenario range for Tiger's fourth quarter.

UP Fintech is expected to report fourth-quarter results in March 2027.

title: Galaxy Withdraws Call That Bitcoin’s Bear Market Ended in June
summary:
Bitcoin Magazine

Galaxy Withdraws Call That Bitcoin’s Bear Market Ended in June
Galaxy Research withdrew its October call that bitcoin's bear market ended in June and said a daily close below $58,525 would signal a move to a materially lower low.
This post Galaxy Withdraws Call That Bitcoin’s Bear ...
content:
Galaxy has withdrawn its October call that bitcoin’s bear market ended in June, saying the technical signal behind it failed after seven straight weeks of losses and that the bear market is “very likely not over.”

Alex Thorn, Galaxy’s head of firmwide research, laid out the reversal in a report published Wednesday and sent to clients a day earlier. “We withdraw our call that the bear market ended in June,” the report said. “The signal it rested on has failed.”

The firm’s Oct. 26 note had argued that bitcoin had entered an accumulation phase. Galaxy said at the time that a weekly close back below the 50-week moving average that was not regained within a month would invalidate its technical case.

That is what happened. Bitcoin closed the week ended Nov. 8 at $74,968, 0.7% below the 50-week average, after seven weekly closes above it. It then closed the week ended Nov. 15 below the 200-week average, which Galaxy has described as the floor of past bear markets.

Galaxy points to $58,525

The week ended Nov. 22 closed at $61,104, 17.9% below the 50-week average and 10.4% below the 200-week average of $68,159. Bitcoin traded below its July 1 intraday low on Nov. 20 and reached $55,100 on Nov. 21, but the June 30 closing low of $58,525 held on a daily basis through Nov. 22.

Galaxy now treats that level as the line to watch. A daily close below $58,525 would be “the start of a move to a materially lower low,” the report said, and the firm would not treat such a close as a buying signal by itself.

History is not kind to breaks like that. In the seven prior bear market cases where bitcoin closed below a low that had stood for at least 60 days, the eventual low was at least 17% lower, with a median of 52%. Applied to the June low, that works out to about $48,500 and $28,200.

Bitcoin briefly slumped below $57,500 on Wednesday morning as the Nasdaq sank, but it ended the day back above $60,000 and has not posted a daily close below $58,525. It traded near $60,800 on Thursday morning.

Late by the clock, early by the depth

Galaxy said two readings of the market disagree. By the calendar, this bear is old: Nov. 22 was day 412 since the Oct. 6, 2025, record, longer than the 163 to 406 days from high to low in the four prior bear markets.

By depth, it looks unfinished. Bitcoin’s 53% decline compares with drops of 77% to 93% in earlier bears. It also has not closed a day below its realized price of $53,205, something every prior bear did for at least 140 days, and only two of the 13 bottom signals Galaxy tracks have been met.

“The clock says this bear is overdue to end, the depth says it has further to fall, and we do not believe the price record alone can settle which,” the report said.

Flows have not helped. Galaxy estimates U.S. spot bitcoin ETPs hold about 1.24 million BTC, 9.7% below their October 2025 peak, after shedding 71,339 BTC, or $4.95 billion, since Oct. 4. November is shaping up as a record month for ETF outflows.

Galaxy said the other three parts of its October thesis, covering positioning, fundamentals and sentiment, are stronger now than when it published. Its proprietary Bitcoin Fear & Greed Index fell to 5.2 on Nov. 21, its lowest reading since June 30, 2022.

To swing back toward its October view, Galaxy wants a weekly close above the 200-week average and then the 50-week average, now $74,401, with the June weekly closing low of $59,517 holding. A weekly close below realized price would point to a deeper bear.

“We are not trying to call the low,” the report said. “Until one gives way, we will judge the market on weekly closes rather than headlines.”

Micah Zimmerman

Micah first discovered Bitcoin in 2018 but remained a skeptic on the sidelines for too long. Since 2021, he has covered crypto and business and now works as a news reporter for Bitcoin Magazine, based in North Carolina.

summary:

Disclaimer

  • Finalto wins two top awards at Finance Magnates Summit London 2026.

London, United Kingdom, November 2026 – Finalto, the bespoke liquidity and fintech provider, has been recognised with two awards at Finance Magnates Summit London 2026, winning Best Liquidity Provider and Best White Label Solution.

The awards were presented during the 15th edition of Finance Magnates Summit London, one of the industry's leading events for brokers, fintech providers, liquidity venues and institutional market participants. Held on 24th November at Old Billingsgate, the summit brought together financial services professionals from across the global trading ecosystem.

The Best Liquidity Provider award represents a significant achievement for Finalto and recognises the firm's ongoing commitment to delivering deep liquidity, competitive pricing, reliable execution and dedicated client support. Over the years, Finalto has received multiple industry awards for its liquidity offering, reflecting a consistent track record of excellence and innovation in serving brokers, institutions and professional traders worldwide.

Finalto was also awarded Best White Label Solution, highlighting the strength of its technology offering and its ability to help brokers launch and scale their businesses through flexible, institutional-grade trading infrastructure.

"Winning both Best Liquidity Provider and Best White Label Solution is a tremendous honour for our team," said Paul Groves, UK CEO at Finalto. "These awards reflect our continued investment in technology, liquidity and client service, as well as the trust our clients place in us. We remain committed to delivering innovative solutions that help our partners succeed in an increasingly competitive market."

During the event, Sam Horowitz, Group Head of Liquidity at Finalto, participated in the panel discussion, "Be the Bank? Prime-of-Prime vs Direct Institutional Access", where industry experts explored the evolving liquidity landscape and the growing demand for institutional-grade market access. An Executive Committee Member of ACI UK Financial Markets Association, Horowitz also continues to support the development of the next generation of financial markets professionals through industry engagement and knowledge sharing. Find out more on how Sam Horowitz supports his team’s development here

The dual recognition at Finance Magnates Summit London reinforces Finalto's position as a trusted partner to financial institutions, brokers and professional traders, combining award-winning liquidity with cutting-edge technology solutions tailored to clients' evolving needs.

title: The Black Friday LTV Trap: Is the Brokerage Industry Buying the Wrong Growth?
summary:
Every November, the brokerage industry takes a page out of the retail playbook. Deposit bonuses get bigger, cashback offers become more generous, and the competition for first-time deposits intensifies.
By Friday afternoon, the acquisition dashboard can make for impressive reading. FTDs are up, acqu...
content:
Every November, the brokerage industry takes a page out of the retail playbook. Deposit bonuses get bigger, cashback offers become more generous, and the competition for first-time deposits intensifies.

By Friday afternoon, the acquisition dashboard can make for impressive reading. FTDs are up, acquisition costs are down, and trading volumes are climbing.

Fast forward 90 days, and a different set of numbers starts to matter.

How many of those traders are still active? Has the revenue generated justified the acquisition cost? Would they have chosen the broker without the incentive?

The brokerage industry has become exceptionally good at measuring the cost of acquiring a trader. It is arguably less effective at measuring the cost of acquiring the wrong one.

Black Friday brings that distinction into sharp focus. Are brokers building customer lifetime value (LTV), or simply buying short-term performance?

Cheaper Acquisition. More Expensive Growth.

Few metrics command as much attention in brokerage marketing as the first-time deposit. Campaigns are optimised around it, affiliate remuneration is often tied to it, and commercial teams use it as a benchmark for growth.

Yet a deposit is not revenue, and a funded account is not necessarily a sustainable client relationship.

There is a principle in economics known as Goodhart's Law: when a measure becomes a target, it can cease to be a useful measure.

An acquisition ecosystem designed and rewarded primarily around generating FTDs will naturally become effective at generating them, irrespective of what happens afterwards.

A campaign that reduces acquisition costs by 30% may appear more efficient. But if the acquired cohort generates substantially less net revenue over its lifetime, that efficiency may be superficial.

The problem is not the FTD as a metric, but the commercial decisions made when it is viewed in isolation. A lower cost per acquisition is only an advantage if the economics of the acquired customer justify it.

The Economics of Who You Acquire

Promotional incentives influence not only conversion rates but also the composition of the customer base.

A trader attracted by a substantial deposit match may have different motivations from one attracted by competitive pricing, execution quality or trading technology. Both register as an FTD, but applying identical lifetime value assumptions to both cohorts could be a costly mistake.

This introduces a potential adverse selection problem: the mechanism designed to make acquisition more efficient may disproportionately attract customers whose primary consideration is the incentive itself.

A campaign optimised around bonus uptake is likely to identify traders who value bonuses. Whether it is equally effective at identifying traders who value the brokerage is another matter.

Of course, a promotion-led customer can become a loyal, high-value client. The distinction lies in whether the promotion removes a barrier to choosing the product or becomes the principal reason for choosing it.

When Bonuses Change Trading Behaviour

The commercial implications of bonuses extend beyond acquisition.

A July 2026 study by Traders Union, surveying 1,450 Forex and CFD traders across six regions, found that 44% of bonus users reported trading more frequently, while 42% said promotional requirements encouraged them to trade more than originally planned.

What stands out is that increased trading frequency was considerably more prevalent than increased leverage.

If activity is driven by promotional conditions rather than a trader's independent assessment of market opportunities, how much of it can reasonably be expected to continue once the incentive expires?

While the research does not establish a direct relationship between bonuses and lower LTV, it highlights the limitations of using promotional trading activity as a proxy for sustainable engagement.

If incentives encourage traders to operate beyond their intended strategy, immediate increases in volume may come at the expense of longer, more sustainable client relationships.

Is Black Friday Creating Demand or Borrowing It?

One of the least visible costs of promotional campaigns is the subsidisation of demand that already exists.

Consider a trader who intends to open an account in December. A Black Friday bonus brings that decision forward. The broker records an additional FTD in November but may simply have paid to acquire a customer it would have acquired organically.

This is the distinction between attribution and incrementality. A campaign can receive credit for a conversion without being responsible for creating it.

The same principle applies when assessing Black Friday's impact on financial markets. Record retail sales, like record FTDs, may reflect demand brought forward rather than genuine growth.

Repeated promotions can compound the problem. Black Friday becomes Christmas, Christmas becomes New Year, and traders begin adjusting their funding decisions accordingly.

Why deposit today when a better offer could arrive next month?

The broker may end up paying to activate demand that its own promotional strategy has encouraged to wait.

When Exceptional Becomes Expected

In behavioural economics, reference dependence describes how people evaluate outcomes relative to an established benchmark. Applied to brokerage marketing, an exceptional offer can gradually become an expected one.

Each new campaign must then compete not only with other brokers but also with the expectations established by previous campaigns.

A deposit bonus can be matched. A cashback offer can be outbid. A discount code can be undercut.

The vulnerability lies in dependency. When incentives become the primary source of differentiation, maintaining acquisition performance can require increasingly generous offers without any corresponding improvement in the underlying product.

In effect, the broker risks renting customer loyalty rather than building it.

The Opportunity Cost of Free Money

There is a fundamental difference between offering someone additional capital to open a trading account and improving the economics of using that account.

A temporary deposit bonus influences the immediate funding decision. Competitive spreads, lower commissions and reliable execution matter throughout the trading relationship.

Every promotional budget, therefore, represents a capital allocation decision.

What generates greater lifetime value: another deposit bonus or an improvement in liquidity infrastructure? A temporary commission discount or a permanent reduction in trading costs?

The answer will depend on the business, but product improvements can strengthen acquisition and retention simultaneously, benefiting existing and prospective clients.

At EC Markets, we view investment in execution technology, liquidity aggregation, competitive pricing and platform development as much as a customer acquisition and retention strategy as a product strategy.

Promotions have a legitimate place within that strategy. But their role should be to amplify the value of the underlying product, not become the primary source of that value.

Bottom Line

Perhaps the brokerage industry needs to reconsider when it declares a Black Friday campaign a success.

The more meaningful assessment comes 90 or 180 days later, when brokers can compare promotional and non-promotional cohorts against retention, second-deposit rates, incentive-adjusted revenue, acquisition payback periods and post-promotion activity.

Black Friday can be an effective acquisition mechanism. The danger lies in confusing the effectiveness of that mechanism with the strength of the business it is acquiring customers for.

A promotion can give a trader a reason to join. The product, technology, trading conditions and client experience must ultimately give them a reason to stay.

The strongest reason to choose a broker shouldn't come with an expiry date.

title: Brazil’s stock exchange pushes stablecoin launch back to 2027
summary: Brazil’s stock exchange is working with six major financial institutions on a real-backed stablecoin that could launch as early as the first quarter of 2027.
content:
Brazil’s stock exchange B3 is moving ahead with 2027 plans for a stablecoin pegged to the Brazilian real, after initially targeting a launch this year.

B3 is collaborating with six of Brazil’s largest financial institutions, Bradesco, BTG Pactual, Itaú Unibanco, Safra, Santander and XP, to launch the stablecoin in the first quarter of 2027, according to a Friday report by local news outlet Valor Econômico.

Called Open BRL, the stablecoin is to be issued by Banco B3, the exchange’s banking subsidiary, with each token backed by one Brazilian real. B3 will operate the underlying technology.

The initiative marks a new stage in the exchange’s digital asset strategy as Brazil’s financial industry prepares to bring traditional securities onto blockchain networks.

B3’s stablecoin plans stretch into 2027

B3 first disclosed plans to introduce its own stablecoin in December 2025, targeting a launch in 2026.

As recently as July, the exchange was reportedly still preparing to launch a stablecoin called B3RL in the coming months, with infrastructure testing and integration with financial institutions scheduled for August and September.

B3RL was designed to be backed by Brazilian reais and secured by government bonds, and to facilitate blockchain-based trading of stocks and fixed-income securities starting in 2027.

It remains unclear whether Open BRL will replace B3RL or operate alongside it. Cointelegraph reached out to B3 for clarification but had not received a response by publication.

Tokenized stocks face regulatory hurdles

B3 also plans to introduce trading of tokenized shares in early 2027, initially using the same order book as conventional equities.

The platform would initially retain its two-business-day settlement cycle rather than introduce instant settlement, Humberto Costa, a B3 executive overseeing digital asset products, reportedly said in October.

Related: Brazil’s Halloween eve crypto deadline brings more tricks than treats

Costa also said B3RL would not handle settlement of tokenized shares at launch and that round-the-clock trading would require changes to Brazil’s regulatory framework.

Brazil’s Securities and Exchange Commission has been exploring a new regulatory framework for tokenization, presenting the progress of its dedicated working group at an industry meeting in October.

title: Match-Trade Appoints Michał Copiuk as CEO as Michał Karczewski Steps Down After Nearly 10 Years
summary:
Match-Trade
Technologies has appointed Michal Copiuk as Chief Executive Officer, effective
December 1, 2026. He replaces Michal Karczewski, who is leaving the company
after nearly ten years.
Copiuk joins from XTB
Group, where he spent 14 years developing its institutional business. He
previously ser...
content:
2026-11-27T14:06:18.420+02:00

Friday, 27/11/2026 | 12:06 GMT by Tareq Sikder

  • Copiuk joins Match-Trade after 14 years leading institutional business at XTB Group.
  • The new CEO brings nearly 20 years of experience in banking, strategy consulting and trading.

Match-Trade Technologies has appointed Michal Copiuk as Chief Executive Officer, effective December 1, 2026. He replaces Michal Karczewski, who is leaving the company after nearly ten years.

Copiuk joins from XTB Group, where he spent 14 years developing its institutional business. He previously served as Chief Executive Officer of X Open Hub, the group's institutional liquidity and execution business, and as Institutional Business Development Director at XTB.

Copiuk Built XTB's Institutional Partner Network

Copiuk has close to 20 years of experience across banking, strategy consulting and the trading industry. During his time at XTB, he helped develop X Open Hub and XTB Institutional into a network of more than 100 technology and liquidity partners across five continents.

At Match-Trade Technologies, Copiuk will focus on developing the business, maintaining existing client relationships, attracting new clients and introducing products. He will also oversee the company's international expansion.

"Match-Trade Technologies has what many companies in this industry lack: full control over its own technology, a large team of outstanding specialists, and the ability to respond quickly to clients' needs," Copiuk said.

Karczewski Leaves After Nearly a Decade

During Karczewski's tenure, Match-Trade Technologies developed from a white-label trading technology provider into a multi-product group. Its businesses now include Match-Trader, its proprietary trading platform, Match-Prime, its liquidity provider, and Match2Pay, its cryptocurrency payments business.

Match-Trader also expanded beyond its white-label offering to include a full server licence. The company entered the proprietary trading sector early, with its platform subsequently adopted by several established firms.

Karczewski said he was leaving to pursue a new chapter outside fintech.

He added that he believed the company was in good condition and expressed confidence in Copiuk's ability to lead it.

Match-Trade Technologies has appointed Michal Copiuk as Chief Executive Officer, effective December 1, 2026. He replaces Michal Karczewski, who is leaving the company after nearly ten years.

Copiuk joins from XTB Group, where he spent 14 years developing its institutional business. He previously served as Chief Executive Officer of X Open Hub, the group's institutional liquidity and execution business, and as Institutional Business Development Director at XTB.

Copiuk Built XTB's Institutional Partner Network

Copiuk has close to 20 years of experience across banking, strategy consulting and the trading industry. During his time at XTB, he helped develop X Open Hub and XTB Institutional into a network of more than 100 technology and liquidity partners across five continents.

At Match-Trade Technologies, Copiuk will focus on developing the business, maintaining existing client relationships, attracting new clients and introducing products. He will also oversee the company's international expansion.

"Match-Trade Technologies has what many companies in this industry lack: full control over its own technology, a large team of outstanding specialists, and the ability to respond quickly to clients' needs," Copiuk said.

Karczewski Leaves After Nearly a Decade

During Karczewski's tenure, Match-Trade Technologies developed from a white-label trading technology provider into a multi-product group. Its businesses now include Match-Trader, its proprietary trading platform, Match-Prime, its liquidity provider, and Match2Pay, its cryptocurrency payments business.

Match-Trader also expanded beyond its white-label offering to include a full server licence. The company entered the proprietary trading sector early, with its platform subsequently adopted by several established firms.

Karczewski said he was leaving to pursue a new chapter outside fintech.

He added that he believed the company was in good condition and expressed confidence in Copiuk's ability to lead it.

title: BASIS Opens First-Round Applications for Card Offering Cashback in the Asset Spent
summary: Victoria, Seychelles, 27th November 2026, Chainwire
content:
Skip to content

Victoria, Seychelles, 27th November 2026, Chainwire

Victoria, Seychelles, November 27th, 2026, Chainwire

Available in Standard and Platinum editions, the BASIS Card offers up to 10% cashback, with applicants selecting their preferred tier subject to staking eligibility

The BASIS Card returns money differently. Announced today by BASIS DIGITAL INFRASTRUCTURE LTD, the payment card credits cashback in the asset used for each eligible purchase, with Platinum cardholders qualifying for 10% cashback during the introductory Launch Boost period.

For digital asset holders, the principle is straightforward. Spend Bitcoin and receive Bitcoin back. Pay with Ethereum and receive Ethereum back. There are no reward points to redeem or proprietary platform tokens to manage. Cashback is credited in an asset the cardholder already uses, giving everyday spending a direct connection to their digital asset holdings.

The opening of first-round applications marks an expansion of BASIS’s existing digital asset infrastructure into everyday payments. Applications are submitted at https://basis.pro/card and close on December 31, 2026, at 23:59 UTC.

Two Card Editions With Different Levels of Benefits

The BASIS Card is available in Standard, finished in matte black composite, and Platinum, produced in metal. Applicants select their preferred edition when submitting their waitlist application, with qualification determined by their active staking position.

Each edition has a separate staking eligibility threshold, as detailed below. BASIS measures the value of the applicant’s active staking position against the requirement for their selected tier. The position is assessed at submission and re-checked at the close of the application period.

Participants can therefore review the benefits of each edition alongside its staking requirements before deciding which card to apply for. Final issuance remains subject to the issuing partner’s independent review.

Card Fees, Cashback, and Launch Boost Benefits

Both editions feature an introductory Launch Boost period, beginning on the date of card issuance. During this period, cardholders receive enhanced cashback rates, higher monthly reward caps, and additional subscription benefits.

*All monetary figures are expressed in USD. Physical card issuance fees include applicable shipping charges.

Launch Boost runs for three months following issuance, after which each card returns to its respective base benefits. Standard and Platinum also feature rate-lock periods of 12 and 24 months, respectively, subject to the applicable program terms.

Along with cashback, the card program brings together subscription rebates of 50% or 100%, depending on the edition and benefit period, across a catalog of over 80 subscriptions. Travel and additional card benefits include two annual airport lounge visits, a 3 GB eSIM, and one additional card, subject to tier eligibility and applicable terms. Standard cardholders benefit from a 2% FX fee, while Platinum cardholders pay no FX fee during Launch Boost. Both editions provide immediate access to a virtual card upon activation, with Platinum participants also receiving priority and dedicated support.

Paid Back in the Asset You Spent

The defining feature of the BASIS Card is what happens after a purchase. Where conventional reward programs may require cardholders to accumulate points or convert rewards into their preferred currency, BASIS keeps the cashback denomination consistent with the asset spent.

Cashback on eligible settled purchases is credited directly to the cardholder’s Funding Wallet. A purchase made using BTC returns BTC, leaving the recipient free to decide how to use the reward.

Cardholders who wish to stake their cashback can do so separately under the platform’s ordinary conversion rules. Cashback does not automatically enter an existing staking position, and card rewards remain independent of staking yield.

Submitting a card application also leaves existing staking positions, lock-up periods, Dynamic Reward Rates, boosters, and stToken balances unchanged.

First-Round Applications and Card Issuance

Applications are free and limited to one per account during Round 01. Participants must hold at least USD 1,000 in eligible BASIS wallet value at submission, maintain an account in good standing, and satisfy the staking requirements for their selected card edition.

Once BASIS approves a waitlist application, the applicant receives further instructions and a secure Know Your Customer (KYC) verification link. The issuing partner then conducts its own review, covering identity verification, residency, regional eligibility, sanctions screening, and supporting documentation.

Waitlist approval permits applicants to proceed to the next stage and does not constitute final card approval, activation, or issuance.

Further information on card eligibility, benefits, fees, and application requirements is available in the official BASIS Card Program documentation.

About BASIS

BASIS DIGITAL INFRASTRUCTURE LTD is a Seychelles international business company (LEI: 254900IX2F2KCWNSSS64) operating market-neutral yield infrastructure, including execution, risk-management, and settlement systems for digital asset staking.

The company holds ISO/IEC 27001:2022 and ISO/IEC 20000-1:2018 certification, both verifiable through IAF CertSearch.

Technical documentation is available at docs.basis.pro.

Base cashback rates are fixed for 12 months on Standard and 24 months on Platinum. Launch Boost rates may be adjusted after the boost period with 30 days’ notice. Both are separate from platform staking rewards, which vary with market conditions.

Card enquiries: [email protected]

summary:

  • FM Academy partners with Chrysothemi Valanidou, launching a free course on Cyprus betting regulations on 3 December 2026.

The collaboration strengthens FM Academy's network of industry experts, bringing legal, regulatory and business expertise to professional education across the betting and gaming sector.

Finance Magnates Academy is pleased to announce its collaboration with Chrysothemi Valanidou, lawyer, business solutions consultant, professional trainer and Founder of Startwise Ltd.

This collaboration forms part of FM Academy's ongoing commitment to bringing experienced industry professionals and subject matter experts into its educational network, supporting professional development and providing access to practical, industry-specific knowledge.

With more than ten years of experience in the betting and gaming industry, Chrysothemi brings extensive expertise in legal, regulatory and operational matters. She previously served as CEO of a licensed betting operator in Cyprus, where she was responsible for management, legal, corporate governance, compliance and regulatory affairs.

A member of the Cyprus Bar Association since 2015, Chrysothemi specialises in betting and gaming licensing, Anti-Money Laundering (AML), responsible gaming, advertising and marketing regulations, and corporate law.

She is also the Founder and Director of Startwise Ltd, through which she advises businesses on strategy, business development, corporate matters and marketing, with a focus on helping organisations meet legal and regulatory requirements.

“I strongly believe that professional education should bridge the gap between theory and practice. Through my collaboration with FM Academy, I look forward to sharing my industry experience and equipping professionals with practical knowledge that enables them to navigate an increasingly complex regulatory and business environment with confidence.”

Combining her legal background with hands-on industry experience, Chrysothemi also designs and delivers professional training programmes, helping individuals and organisations better understand regulatory frameworks and their practical application in business.

First Educational Initiative: Free Course on the Future of Betting in Cyprus

As the first initiative under this collaboration, Finance Magnates Academy will introduce a free online training session titled The Future of Betting in Cyprus: Regulatory Perspectives, led by Chrysothemi Valanidou.

Taking place on 3 December 2026, from 16:00 to 17:00 Cyprus time, the one-hour session will examine the key legal and regulatory requirements affecting betting operators in Cyprus.

The course will cover the Cyprus Betting Law and the role of the National Betting Authority, AML obligations, advertising and marketing regulations, influencer marketing, sponsorship and player protection.

Participants will gain a better understanding of the regulatory framework governing licensed betting operators, common compliance challenges and the changes shaping the industry's future.

The free session is designed for betting operator executives, compliance and AML professionals, legal advisers, marketing teams and other professionals working within or alongside the betting and gaming industry.

title: ATFX Connect Marks New Chapter with London Office Relocation
summary:
ATFX Connect, the institutional multi-asset brokerage and liquidity provider of ATFX Group, has celebrated its relocation to a new office in London. The relocation strengthens the company’s existing presence in the UK and supports its continued development of its institutional business.

Disclaimer

  • ATFX Connect celebrates its new London office relocation.

ATFX Connect, the institutional multi-asset brokerage and liquidity provider of ATFX Group, has celebrated its relocation to a new office in London. The relocation strengthens the company’s existing presence in the UK and supports its continued development of its institutional business.

The move was marked by an exclusive networking reception at City Social in Tower 42, bringing together ATFX Group’s senior leadership, clients, business partners and industry representatives. The new office provides closer engagement with institutional clients and industry partners in one of the world’s leading financial centres.

Leadership Marks a New Chapter for ATFX Connect

The opening celebration featured welcome remarks from Wei Qiang Zhang, Managing Director of ATFX Connect Global, followed by an address from Joe Li, Chairman of ATFX Group. Both highlighted the significance of the new office and its contribution to ATFX Connect's continued development.

In his address, Joe Li highlighted London's importance to ATFX Group's international development and the value of maintaining a local presence in key financial markets.

“London remains an important centre for the global financial industry, and strengthening our presence here is an important part of ATFX Group's long-term development. The relocation of ATFX Connect's UK office reflects our commitment to building a stronger international business and deepening our relationships across key financial markets. We believe that a strong local presence, supported by our global capabilities, is essential to creating sustainable opportunities for the Group,” said Joe Li, Chairman of ATFX Group.

Wei Qiang Zhang, Managing Director of ATFX Connect Global, added: “The move to our new UK office represents an important step forward for ATFX Connect. Having a dedicated presence in London allows us to further strengthen our engagement with institutional clients and industry partners in this important market. As we continue to develop our institutional business, our focus remains on building long-term relationships and delivering solutions that address the evolving needs of our clients.”

Bringing the Industry Together

The celebration brought together members of ATFX Group's senior management team, including Joe Li, Wei Qiang Zhang, Drew Niv, Chief Strategy Officer of ATFX, Weems Chan, Global Head of Marketing, and Hui Zhu, Global Head of Legal and Compliance.

Following the leadership speeches, senior representatives joined the official toast to commemorate the opening, followed by a group photograph. Guests then continued the evening with live music, refreshments, and networking.

Supporting ATFX Connect's Continued Institutional Development

As the institutional business of ATFX Group, ATFX Connect provides multi-asset brokerage and liquidity solutions to institutional clients. Its London office supports closer engagement with clients and industry partners as the company continues to develop its institutional business and build its presence in key financial markets.

About ATFX Connect

ATFX Connect is a trading name of AT Global Markets (UK) Ltd, AT Global Markets (Australia) Pty Ltd, AT Global Financial Services (HK) Ltd, ATFX Global Markets (CY) Ltd, AT Global Markets Intl Ltd, AT Global Markets SA (PTY) Ltd, and all are part of the ATFX Group.

ATFX Connect is a global multi-asset brokerage and liquidity provider, offering institutional and professional investors an extensive range of services, from agency liquidity, prime brokerage and post-trade clearing, to margin trading liquidity in OTC derivatives.

For further information on ATFX Connect, please visit ATFX Connect website https://www.atfxconnect.com.
