title: Zcash Developers Race to Secure Crypto. Can Quantum Computing Break Bitcoin?
summary: Key takeaways Zcash development team Zakura (November 26) called for accelerated retirement of the older Sapling privacy pool, which it estimated held about 400,000 ZEC. A November 27 dashboard snapshot showed about 306,684 ZEC still in Sapling, though that does not prove the warning prompted anyone...
content:
Key takeaways

  • Zcash development team Zakura (November 26) called for accelerated retirement of the older Sapling privacy pool, which it estimated held about 400,000 ZEC.
  • A November 27 dashboard snapshot showed about 306,684 ZEC still in Sapling, though that does not prove the warning prompted anyone to move funds.
  • Zakura’s concern is speculative, unverified mathematical advances, not a successful quantum attack, and Shielded Labs expects to pick a post-quantum direction by the end of January 2027.
  • The Quantum Ledger counts about 7.23 million BTC (35.9% of issued supply) with public keys already visible on-chain; Glassnode’s May estimate was 6.04 million BTC.
  • No reliable date exists for a quantum computer that can break crypto signatures, but upgrading blockchains, wallets and custody could itself take years.

Can quantum computing break crypto? For years, the question has largely been treated as a problem for the distant future. Zcash developers, however, are already discussing what to do with hundreds of thousands of coins that could become vulnerable if certain cryptographic protections fail.

On November 26, Zcash development team Zakura called for the accelerated retirement of Sapling, an older privacy system that the team estimated still held around 400,000 ZEC. The recommendation followed speculation about mathematical breakthroughs at artificial intelligence laboratories.

A day earlier, Shielded Labs published its first technical update on a separate project designed to protect Zcash against future quantum computers.

Neither development means cryptocurrency has been cracked. Together, however, they raise a more pressing question: can blockchain developers replace the mathematics protecting investors’ money before someone finds a way around it?

What Is Quantum Computing?

Quantum computing is a way of processing information using the properties of quantum mechanics. Unlike conventional computers, which represent information using bits with a value of either zero or one, quantum computers operate using quantum bits, commonly known as qubits.

By manipulating these qubits, researchers can design algorithms capable of solving certain mathematical problems far more efficiently than conventional computers.

The important word here is certain. A quantum computer is not simply a faster version of the laptop sitting on your desk. Its advantages depend on the type of problem it is trying to solve.

Unfortunately for the cryptocurrency industry, some of those problems underpin the security of digital wallets.

As explained in NewsBTC’s guide to quantum computing, blockchains rely on cryptographic signatures to establish ownership and authorize transactions. A sufficiently powerful quantum computer could undermine some of the signature systems currently used to protect digital assets.

How Could Quantum Computers Steal Cryptocurrency?

When you send Bitcoin from your wallet, the network needs to establish that you have the authority to spend those coins. It does this by verifying a digital signature produced using your private key.

Your private key is supposed to remain secret. The corresponding public key can be disclosed because working backward from a public key to its private counterpart is computationally impractical using conventional methods.

Quantum computing could change that.

In 1994, mathematician Peter Shor introduced a quantum algorithm that could efficiently solve certain mathematical problems underlying modern public-key cryptography.

A sufficiently powerful quantum computer running such an algorithm could potentially recover private keys from exposed public keys. An attacker could then create a transaction that the blockchain would recognize as valid, even though the original owner had never authorized it.

That is a particularly uncomfortable problem for cryptocurrencies. Bitcoin does not have a customer service department that can reverse an unauthorized transfer.

The National Institute of Standards and Technology has already developed alternative cryptographic standards intended to withstand these future attacks. The challenge for crypto is incorporating such protection into networks that were originally built around different assumptions.

How Much Bitcoin Is Exposed to Quantum Computing?

Bitcoin’s public transaction history makes it possible to estimate how much of its supply could be exposed under certain quantum attack scenarios.

According to a November 25 snapshot from The Quantum Ledger, approximately 7.23 million BTC, representing 35.9% of issued supply under its methodology, was associated with public keys or spending scripts already visible on the blockchain.

Around 1.94 million BTC was classified as exposed because of its output design. A further 5.29 million BTC was associated with addresses that had previously revealed relevant spending information.

Some of these coins date back to Bitcoin’s earliest years, when transactions commonly revealed public keys directly.

Estimates vary between researchers because they do not all measure exposure in exactly the same way. In May 2026, Glassnode’s research identified 6.04 million BTC under its own classification framework.

These figures should not be interpreted as the amount of Bitcoin that will eventually be stolen. They measure a potential vulnerability under a specific future scenario, not an active attack.

Owners of many exposed coins could migrate their holdings if suitable protection becomes available. Dormant wallets whose owners have lost their private keys present a considerably harder problem.

Why Zcash Developers Want to Retire an Older Privacy System

Zcash offers a useful example of how complicated a cryptographic migration can become.

Unlike Bitcoin, where transactions are generally visible on a public ledger, Zcash provides privacy features through shielded pools. These allow users to transact without publicly revealing certain transaction details.

Sapling is one of the network’s older shielded systems. Its proof mechanism relies on mathematical assumptions that Zakura believes warrant additional scrutiny in light of potentially accelerating cryptographic research.

“

The time to prepare for a cryptographic breakthrough is before it happens.

Zakura · Sapling retirement proposal

Zakura proposed preventing new deposits into Sapling while encouraging users to migrate to Ironwood, a newer privacy system. If credible evidence of a threat emerged, further emergency measures could be considered.

The amount involved is already changing. A November 27 snapshot from the Zcash Dashboard, timestamped 06:06 UTC, showed approximately 306,684 ZEC remaining in Sapling, below the rounded estimate cited in Zakura’s proposal. The difference does not, by itself, establish that the warning prompted users to move their funds.

The discussion follows Zcash’s recent NU7 network upgrade, which improved transaction speed and continued the network’s transition away from older infrastructure.

Importantly, the immediate concern raised by Zakura is not evidence of a successful quantum attack. It relates to speculative advances in mathematics that could affect particular cryptographic constructions. Those advances remain unverified.

Can Zcash Become Quantum-Resistant?

On November 25, Shielded Labs published an update on its Epoch project, which aims to develop privacy technology capable of withstanding future quantum computers.

One of the problems its researchers are working on is the size of cryptographic proofs.

Stronger protection can require considerably more data to be processed and transmitted. That can create difficulties for blockchains, where transaction capacity, verification costs and storage requirements already matter.

The team is evaluating two possible approaches and expects to select a direction by the end of January 2027, provided its research progresses as planned.

Ironwood already incorporates features intended to support a future recovery mechanism. However, the developers have made clear that these features do not make Zcash fully quantum-resistant today.

The distinction is important. Having a contingency plan for a future attack is not the same as having protection against one.

Are Bitcoin and Ethereum Preparing for Quantum Computing?

Zcash is not the only network confronting these issues.

Bitcoin developers are discussing changes through proposals including BIP-360, which would introduce a transaction output format designed to reduce certain forms of public-key exposure.

A separate draft, BIP-361, explores a gradual transition away from vulnerable signature schemes once suitable alternatives are available.

Neither proposal should be confused with an activated Bitcoin upgrade.

Ethereum faces additional complications. Beyond individual wallets, its security model relies on cryptographic signatures used by validators and other infrastructure.

Ethereum’s quantum-security challenge extends to staking arrangements and institutional custody.

There is also a governance problem that applies particularly to Bitcoin. If millions of coins remain in old wallets that cannot be migrated, should the network eventually restrict their movement to prevent potential theft?

Doing so could protect the broader ecosystem, but it could also prevent legitimate owners from accessing their own money. Leaving those coins untouched carries a different set of risks.

Cryptography alone cannot settle that argument.

When Will Quantum Computing Become a Real Threat to Crypto?

There is no reliable date for when a quantum computer capable of breaking widely used cryptocurrency signatures will become available.

Building such a machine requires more than increasing the number of qubits. Those qubits must also be reliable enough to carry out lengthy, complex calculations without errors overwhelming the results.

According to Coinbase Institute’s research, the relevant machines do not yet exist, but the process of upgrading blockchains, wallets and custody infrastructure could itself take years.

For that reason, waiting for an actual attack before implementing stronger cryptography would be a risky approach.

Crypto investors should pay attention to what developers implement, whether wallets support the new protections and whether existing funds can be migrated without compromising ownership.

There is no need to buy a token simply because its developers describe it as quantum-resistant, either. Such claims deserve scrutiny of the underlying cryptography and its implementation.

Zcash’s latest proposals offer a glimpse of the decisions other blockchain communities may eventually face. Replacing an algorithm is one thing. Persuading an entire decentralized financial network to move its money before a deadline is something else entirely.

title: Fidelity Files for Spot Chainlink ETF With Proposed Nasdaq Listing
summary: Fidelity filed to launch a spot Chainlink ETF that would hold LINK directly, skip staking and trade on Nasdaq under the proposed ticker FLNK.
content:
Skip to content
Assets: LINK

Fidelity filed to launch a spot Chainlink ETF that would hold LINK directly, skip staking and trade on Nasdaq under the proposed ticker FLNK.

Fidelity has filed with the US Securities and Exchange Commission to launch a spot Chainlink exchange-traded fund. The proposed Fidelity Chainlink Fund would hold LINK directly and is expected to list on Nasdaq under the ticker FLNK, according to its November 25 registration statement.

The fund would track the price of LINK using a Fidelity reference rate, adjusted for expenses and other liabilities. The preliminary filing leaves some terms, including the sponsor fee, open. The registration must become effective before the fund can sell shares.

Direct LINK holdings without staking

Fidelity named Anchorage Digital Bank, BitGo Bank & Trust and Coinbase Custody as custodians for the fund’s LINK. Authorised participants would be able to create or redeem large blocks of shares using LINK or cash. Investors buying shares on Nasdaq would trade at market prices, which could be higher or lower than the value of the LINK backing each share.

The fund would not stake its LINK. As Fidelity states in the prospectus, “Shareholders will not receive staking rewards through the Trust.” That leaves investors with exposure to the token’s price after fund expenses. Chainlink staking is a separate mechanism in which participants commit LINK to help secure certain network services and can earn rewards.

Fidelity would enter a market that already includes the Grayscale Chainlink Trust ETF, which trades under GLNK. BNC previously covered Grayscale’s application to convert its Chainlink trust into an exchange-traded fund. Fidelity’s fee and other final terms will help determine how the proposed product compares with existing funds.

How Chainlink usage reaches the token

Chainlink supplies blockchain applications with outside information, such as asset prices used by lending protocols to value collateral. It also provides infrastructure for moving data and assets across blockchains. LINK is the network’s native token and is used to pay for services and support staking.

Some users pay for Chainlink services in other currencies or digital assets. Under the network’s payment abstraction system, eligible fees can be converted into LINK. Chainlink says part of that revenue goes into its on-chain reserve. These conversions are one way service usage can produce demand for LINK. Fund shareholders would hold an interest in a trust that owns the token, with no claim on Chainlink’s service revenue.

title: Ethereum’s Co-Founder Takes On Crypto’s Next Security Threat. Who Is Vitalik Buterin?
summary: Key takeaways Vitalik Buterin’s November 26 essay argues that crypto security must extend to the physical chips inside devices, summed up as “Not your silicon, not your keys.” He wants manufacturers to publish physical chip layouts (GDS files) so investigators can compare real hardware against the d...
content:
Key takeaways

  • Vitalik Buterin’s November 26 essay argues that crypto security must extend to the physical chips inside devices, summed up as “Not your silicon, not your keys.”
  • He wants manufacturers to publish physical chip layouts (GDS files) so investigators can compare real hardware against the design.
  • Researcher Andrew Huang’s infrared inspection technique (IRIS) can examine chips without removing them, but it has resolution limits and is not a universal fix.
  • The essay is a proposal, not a claim that existing hardware wallets are compromised, and publishing it does not give Buterin power to change Ethereum unilaterally.
  • Arkham attributes about $390 million in assets to Buterin, mostly roughly 224,000 ETH, though his true net worth is not publicly established.

Who is Vitalik Buterin, and why is Ethereum’s co-founder now questioning the security of the very devices crypto investors use to protect their wealth? The 32-year-old programmer has turned his attention to a problem that even open-source software cannot necessarily solve: compromised computer chips.

In an essay published on November 26, Buterin argued that cryptocurrency security needs to extend beyond software and into the physical hardware on which it runs. His message builds on one of crypto’s oldest principles, but with a new twist:

“

Not your silicon, not your keys.

Vitalik Buterin · Essay, November 26

For someone who helped build an alternative to centralized financial infrastructure, questioning the manufacturers behind that infrastructure seems like a natural next step.

It also reflects a security philosophy that has become increasingly visible in Buterin’s work, from his push for greater privacy and quantum safety on Ethereum’s roadmap to his interest in independently verifiable computing.

Who Is Vitalik Buterin?

Vitalik Buterin is a Russian-Canadian programmer, researcher and writer who conceived Ethereum in 2013, at the age of 19.

Born in Russia in 1994 and raised in Canada, Buterin discovered Bitcoin in 2011. He went on to co-found Bitcoin Magazine, where he explored the technology and economics behind cryptocurrencies long before digital assets attracted mainstream financial institutions.

His involvement in Bitcoin exposed him to a problem that would eventually lead to Ethereum. Blockchain technology had potential beyond transferring money, but building more sophisticated applications on Bitcoin presented technical limitations.

Rather than trying to accommodate every possible application within Bitcoin’s existing architecture, Buterin began working on a blockchain designed specifically for programmability.

At the time, he was studying computer science at the University of Waterloo, where he also worked as a research assistant to cryptographer Ian Goldberg.

According to the University of Waterloo, Buterin received a $100,000 Thiel Fellowship in 2014 and subsequently left university to work on Ethereum full-time.

How Vitalik Buterin Created Ethereum

In November 2013, Buterin wrote the initial draft of what would become the Ethereum whitepaper.

The proposal described a blockchain with a general-purpose programming environment. Developers would no longer need to create an entirely new network every time they wanted to build a decentralized application.

Consider a lending platform. Instead of relying on a bank to manage collateral, calculate interest and authorize withdrawals, developers could encode those rules into smart contracts running on Ethereum.

That does not eliminate every risk. Smart contracts can contain bugs, depend on unreliable external data or operate under centralized administrative controls. What Ethereum introduced was the ability to execute financial and other programmable agreements on a shared blockchain.

Although Buterin originated the concept, Ethereum was not built by him alone. Its founding team included seven other individuals: Gavin Wood, Joseph Lubin, Charles Hoskinson, Anthony Di Iorio, Mihai Alisie, Jeffrey Wilcke and Amir Chetrit.

The project’s first live network, known as Frontier, launched on July 30, 2015.

What began as an experimental computing platform eventually became the foundation for much of the decentralized finance industry. Stablecoins, decentralized exchanges, lending protocols and tokenized financial assets now use the infrastructure that Buterin and Ethereum’s early contributors helped establish.

The network’s own evolution, particularly its transition to proof-of-stake and the development of Layer 2 scaling networks, has shaped Ethereum’s first decade.

Vitalik Buterin’s Latest Warning: Can Crypto Wallets Really Be Trusted?

A hardware wallet is supposed to keep private keys away from potentially compromised computers and smartphones. But what happens if the device itself cannot be trusted?

Buterin’s latest research examines that possibility. He points to supply chain attacks involving tampered wallets and considers the potential for malicious modifications concealed inside apparently legitimate chips.

Open-source firmware allows researchers to examine the instructions a device runs. But those instructions reveal little about whether the manufactured chip has been altered.

Buterin wants manufacturers to disclose physical chip layouts, known as GDS files, so investigators have a reference against which to inspect actual hardware.

The distinction matters. Knowing what a chip is designed to do is not necessarily the same as knowing what the chip inside your wallet actually does.

The Technology That Could Help Detect Compromised Chips

One approach highlighted by Buterin comes from hardware security researcher Andrew Huang, better known as bunnie.

Huang has been developing a technique called Infra-Red, In Situ inspection (IRIS), which exploits the fact that silicon becomes transparent at certain infrared wavelengths.

Using infrared illumination and suitable imaging equipment, researchers can examine parts of a chip’s internal structure without necessarily removing it from its circuit board.

The technique could help detect substituted components or unexpected differences between manufactured chips and their intended designs.

However, it is not a universal solution.

In a 2024 update on his research, Huang explained that infrared imaging has resolution limits. It cannot reliably reveal every microscopic feature of modern chips. Combining imaging with additional electrical testing could improve confidence in a component’s integrity.

That is an important limitation for crypto investors. Publishing an open hardware design does not automatically make a wallet secure, just as publishing a smart contract’s code does not establish that it is free of vulnerabilities.

Buterin acknowledges that sophisticated hardware inspections are more likely to be performed by specialist organizations than ordinary wallet owners.

His essay is a proposal for improving security, not an announcement that existing hardware wallets have all been compromised.

Does Vitalik Buterin Control Ethereum?

Despite his status as Ethereum’s most recognizable co-founder, Buterin is not its CEO.

Ethereum is maintained through the participation of independent developers, researchers, node operators, validators and other ecosystem contributors. Changes to the network involve technical proposals, discussion, software development and adoption by participants.

Buterin has considerable influence over those discussions, but publishing a proposal does not give him the authority to implement it unilaterally.

His role within the Ethereum Foundation is also distinct from control over the blockchain itself. In its April 2025 governance announcement, the Foundation described Buterin’s responsibilities as providing technical and intellectual guidance to the wider ecosystem.

His research can influence the direction Ethereum takes. Whether the network ultimately follows that direction depends on considerably more than his endorsement.

How Much Is Vitalik Buterin Worth?

Buterin accumulated considerable wealth through his involvement in Ethereum, with much of his publicly visible cryptocurrency wealth tied to ETH.

However, his exact net worth is not publicly established.

Blockchain analytics can estimate the value of assets held in wallets attributed to him, but those figures do not necessarily account for all his investments, liabilities, private assets or holdings at addresses that have not been publicly identified.

They also fluctuate with cryptocurrency prices. A wallet valuation should therefore not be confused with a complete assessment of his personal wealth.

What Is Vitalik Buterin’s Vision for the Future of Crypto?

Buterin’s latest essay is part of a longer-running interest in making digital infrastructure independently verifiable.

In September 2025, he published The Importance of Full-Stack Openness and Verifiability, exploring how transparency could extend across the hardware and software underpinning increasingly important parts of people’s lives.

His broader research includes cryptography, privacy, blockchain scalability and Ethereum’s transition toward greater quantum resistance. Buterin has previously called for greater experimentation across Ethereum’s application layer without compromising its core principles of censorship resistance, open-source development, privacy and security.

These interests share a practical concern: whether users can independently establish that the systems they rely on behave as intended.

There is a commercial obstacle, though. Semiconductor manufacturers invest heavily in proprietary processes, and designing chips specifically for inspectability can involve performance compromises.

But a device signing a cryptocurrency transaction does not necessarily need the computing power of a modern AI processor. That makes security-focused hardware a potentially useful starting point.

More than a decade ago, Buterin challenged the idea that blockchains should primarily be used to transfer money. His latest work challenges another assumption the industry has grown comfortable with: that trusting the code is enough.

For crypto investors, the next meaningful development may come from hardware manufacturers willing to make their products independently inspectable, rather than another software update promising greater security.

title: US House Panel Advances Bitcoin Reserve Bill With 20-Year Holding Rule
summary: A US House committee advanced a bill to put the Strategic Bitcoin Reserve into federal law and bar sales of Bitcoin held in it for at least 20 years.
content:
Skip to content
Assets: BTC

A US House committee advanced a bill to put the Strategic Bitcoin Reserve into federal law and bar sales of Bitcoin held in it for at least 20 years.

The US House Financial Services Committee has advanced a bill that would put the Strategic Bitcoin Reserve into federal law and require the Treasury to hold Bitcoin deposited in it for at least 20 years from enactment.

The committee reported H.R. 8957, the American Reserve Modernization Act of 2026, with amendments on November 24. The bill was placed on the House Union Calendar, a step that makes it eligible for floor consideration. It still needs to clear the House and Senate and be signed into law. Alaska Republican Rep. Nick Begich introduced the measure in May.

What Treasury could do with the reserve

The bill would direct qualifying Bitcoin already owned by the federal government into the reserve and qualifying non-Bitcoin assets into a separate Digital Asset Stockpile. Treasury would administer both. The bill says reserve assets could not be “sold, swapped, auctioned, encumbered, or otherwise disposed of” during the minimum holding period. The restriction starts on the date the law takes effect and applies to Bitcoin acquired by the US and deposited in the reserve, regardless of how the government obtained it.

Two years before the holding period ends, Treasury would have to recommend whether to keep holding the Bitcoin or allow a gradual release. Once the period expires, the secretary could recommend selling up to 10% of the reserve’s assets in any two-year period.

The bill separately gives Treasury a year from enactment to study when an early sale might be appropriate and recommend any changes to the law, including possible exceptions for national security or financial stability. That study would leave any decision to create an exception with Congress.

How it builds on the 2025 executive order

President Donald Trump established the reserve and stockpile by executive order in March 2025. The order used eligible forfeited Bitcoin as the basis for the reserve and directed the government to retain Bitcoin deposited in it. It also authorised Treasury and Commerce to develop strategies to acquire additional Bitcoin without imposing incremental costs on taxpayers.

The House bill would set the holding rule in statute and create reporting and public proof-of-reserves requirements. It would also give Treasury and Commerce 180 days to study whether the government could acquire more Bitcoin in a way that avoids increasing the national debt. The bill calls for a study and sets no purchase target or acquisition schedule. A separate proposal from Sen. Cynthia Lummis would authorise the government to acquire an additional one million Bitcoin.

The next step is a House floor vote. The Block reported that the approaching end of the 119th Congress leaves limited time for both chambers to act.

title: Michael Saylor’s Net Worth Plunges $6 Billion: The Cost of His Bitcoin Bet
summary: Key takeaways Michael Saylor’s estimated net worth has fallen about $6 billion, from $9.3 billion in October 2025 to roughly $3.3 billion on November 25, 2026, a 64.5% drop per Forbes. The $6 billion is a drop in estimated wealth, not a confirmed cash loss or the proceeds of any asset sales. Saylor’...
content:
Key takeaways

  • Michael Saylor’s estimated net worth has fallen about $6 billion, from $9.3 billion in October 2025 to roughly $3.3 billion on November 25, 2026, a 64.5% drop per Forbes.
  • The $6 billion is a drop in estimated wealth, not a confirmed cash loss or the proceeds of any asset sales.
  • Saylor’s personal 17,732 BTC (bought for about $175 million) would be worth roughly $1.07 billion at $60,325, assuming he still holds them all.
  • Strategy holds 851,305 BTC bought at an average $75,446, leaving a paper shortfall of about $12.88 billion against its $64.23 billion cost.
  • Strategy’s mNAV was 0.94 at the November 25 close, so raising capital by issuing shares has become harder, and that matters as much as the Bitcoin price.

Michael Saylor’s net worth has fallen by approximately $6 billion since the cryptocurrency market peaked in October 2025. The Strategy co-founder, whose fortune was estimated at $9.3 billion at the time, is now worth around $3.3 billion, according to Forbes.

The decline has wiped out nearly two-thirds of Saylor’s estimated wealth. Yet the billionaire’s company continues to accumulate Bitcoin despite mounting paper losses, showing little willingness to reconsider its investment strategy.

For Saylor, the downturn presents a problem that extends well beyond the price of Bitcoin. Much of his fortune depends on a company that must convince investors to keep financing its accumulation strategy.

How Much Has Michael Saylor Lost During the Bitcoin Crash?

Saylor was already among the cryptocurrency industry’s biggest financial casualties in February, when Forbes estimated that his wealth had fallen by $4.7 billion from its October 2025 level.

His fortune briefly stabilized in the following months, reaching an estimated $4.7 billion in June, before suffering another setback.

The latest estimate puts Saylor’s wealth approximately 64.5% below its October 2025 level.

Source: Forbes. Selected valuation snapshots, not daily observations. Hover over a bar for details.

Bitcoin’s return to the $60,000 level has added pressure, but the cryptocurrency alone does not explain the scale of the decline. Saylor’s exposure through Strategy makes his financial position considerably more complicated than that of an ordinary Bitcoin investor.

The $6 billion represents a reduction in estimated wealth, not a confirmed cash loss or the proceeds of any disclosed asset sales.

How Much Bitcoin Does Michael Saylor Personally Own?

In October 2020, Saylor disclosed that he personally owned 17,732 BTC, acquired for approximately $175 million.

At the Bitcoin price of $60,325 reported by Strategy on November 26, those holdings would be worth approximately $1.07 billion, assuming he still owns the entire disclosed amount.

That would leave his original personal investment with an unrealized gain of roughly $895 million.

His current personal Bitcoin balance has not been independently confirmed, but the calculation illustrates an important distinction. Saylor can lose billions in estimated wealth while remaining substantially profitable on his original Bitcoin purchases.

The situation at Strategy is quite different.

Strategy Is Sitting on Nearly $13 Billion in Bitcoin Paper Losses

While Saylor began buying Bitcoin at considerably lower prices, his company has spent much of the past several years increasing its exposure at higher valuations.

According to its November 23 SEC filing, Strategy acquired another 457 BTC for $29.6 million, bringing its total holdings to 851,305 BTC.

The company has spent approximately $64.23 billion accumulating Bitcoin at an average purchase price of $75,446.

Its official Bitcoin dashboard valued those reserves at approximately $51.35 billion on November 26.

That leaves a gap of nearly $12.9 billion between the company’s cumulative acquisition cost and the market value of its Bitcoin holdings.

Strategy Bitcoin portfolio Value
Total holdings 851,305 BTC
Average acquisition price $75,446
Total acquisition cost $64.23 billion
Current Bitcoin reserve value $51.35 billion
Estimated shortfall against cost $12.88 billion

These figures do not represent realized trading losses, nor do they capture the full financial performance of the company.

Nevertheless, the numbers reveal how dramatically the economics of accumulating Bitcoin have changed during the downturn.

Why Saylor’s Fortune Is Vulnerable to More Than Bitcoin

For years, investors were willing to pay a premium for Strategy shares. The attraction was not simply the Bitcoin it owned, but the prospect that management could raise additional capital and increase shareholders’ exposure to the cryptocurrency.

That premium is no longer something the company can take for granted.

Strategy’s dashboard showed an mNAV ratio of 0.94 at the November 25 stock market close, using its own net Bitcoin value per share methodology.

The company’s latest investor briefing acknowledges the implications:

“

A widening discount can cause MSTR to underperform BTC even when bitcoin rises.

Strategy · Investor briefing

This is where Saylor’s investment model faces a more difficult test.

When investors are willing to pay a premium for Strategy shares, raising capital to acquire more Bitcoin can improve the economics of the business. When that premium disappears, issuing additional shares becomes a more complicated proposition.

Strategy’s own sensitivity analysis shows that a Bitcoin price of $40,000 would reduce its estimated net reserve value per share to $45.37, compared with $163.17 at a Bitcoin price of $100,000. The figures illustrate how sensitive the company’s underlying reserve valuation is to Bitcoin price movements.

Strategy’s third-quarter financial results offer a clearer picture of why its cash reserves and financing obligations now matter almost as much as the price of Bitcoin.

Buying more Bitcoin is only one part of the equation. The cost of financing those purchases matters just as much.

Could Michael Saylor’s Net Worth Recover?

There is a credible case for recovery. Strategy still owns more than 850,000 Bitcoin, giving it considerable exposure to any sustained cryptocurrency market rebound.

The company also reported approximately $4.82 billion in combined cash and dollar reserves in its latest investor briefing, providing a buffer against its financing obligations.

But a recovery in Bitcoin would not necessarily produce an equivalent recovery in Saylor’s wealth. Strategy’s share price also depends on its debt, preferred-stock obligations, access to capital and the valuation investors are willing to assign to its business model.

The next test for Saylor is not whether he can buy another thousand Bitcoin. It is whether he can continue financing those purchases on terms that benefit existing shareholders.

His personal fortune has already demonstrated how expensive that distinction can become.

title: GTA VI Is Now a Spectator Sport. Of Course You Can Bet on It
summary: Polymarket logged about $131,000 in trading on when a Twitch streamer would finish GTA VI. Vice City has acquired a betting desk, and the man at the centre of it is playing a video game.
content:
Skip to content

Polymarket logged about $131,000 in trading on when a Twitch streamer would finish GTA VI. Vice City has acquired a betting desk, and the man at the centre of it is playing a video game.

I thought the most Vice City thing you could do this week was drive a stolen car into the ocean and blame the handling. It turns out you can sit at home and take a financial position on when a man called TheBurntPeanut will finish Grand Theft Auto VI. The ocean can wait.

Polymarket displayed about US$131,000 in trading volume on its TheBurntPeanut finish-date market. That’s the value of trades, and the same shares can change hands more than once. Still, it’s a substantial amount of buying and selling over the question of when one Twitch streamer will be done with a video game.

Polymarket’s GTA VI page also lists contracts on when another streamer, ohnePixel, would finish and when Rockstar might release a PC version. The PC one I get. Millions of people would like a date from a company perfectly happy to let them keep asking. The Peanut one is more interesting because nearly everything that makes him worth watching can also make him take longer.

Please proceed directly to the plot

Rockstar spent years building a world in which wandering off is half the pleasure. Some of the best moments in these games start when you miss a turn, hear something good on the radio or decide, on evidence available only to you, that a particular car needs to be in a particular swimming pool. A deadline contract gives somebody watching at home a reason to look at that same swimming pool and think about the time.

Polymarket lists TheBurntPeanut’s Twitch channel as a resolution source. Its contract titles use the word “by,” which matters. Several dates can resolve Yes if he finishes early enough. The deadlines are separate propositions. For the viewer, the difference between finishing a game and continuing to play it is pleasantly blurry. For anybody settling a contract, it has to be sharp enough to pay out on.

Imagine buying Yes on a near deadline and then watching him discover a boat. Before you placed the bet, the boat was good television. You might even have been the person in chat demanding he steal it. Now you have the unfortunate experience of sincerely wanting a man in a video game to ignore a boat. You could have had that feeling for free by becoming somebody’s project manager.

The audience has a position

Sports betting already taught people to watch the last few minutes of a decided game because somebody still needs to score. A streamer’s schedule gives a market looser material. A broadcast can run late, stop early or turn into forty minutes of something the person playing finds hilarious. He’s also close enough to his viewers to read what they type. You can see the potential for a very strange chat window when some of the people in it would prefer he keep moving.

That’s a possibility, and the trading volume tells us about trades. It can’t tell us how a streamer played or why a particular viewer kept watching. The reason this market is worth a look is how cheaply it can change the stakes for the audience. A running joke, a detour, or a decision to call it a night can suddenly have a financial meaning for someone who has absolutely no say in any of it.

I wrote last week about how much ownership you get when you buy GTA VI. There is now a pleasantly absurd alternative. You can buy an interest in how quickly somebody else gets through his copy. I hope he takes the boat.

title: Monero’s Delisting Nightmare Continues: XMR Price Plunges 15%
summary: Key takeaways Monero fell about 15% on Thursday, from $525.36 to $446.54 per BitInfoCharts, after KuCoin announced it will delist XMR. KuCoin will end all four XMR spot pairs on November 30 at 08:00 UTC; deposits are already suspended and withdrawals stay open until December 31. XMR will also stop b...
content:
Key takeaways

  • Monero fell about 15% on Thursday, from $525.36 to $446.54 per BitInfoCharts, after KuCoin announced it will delist XMR.
  • KuCoin will end all four XMR spot pairs on November 30 at 08:00 UTC; deposits are already suspended and withdrawals stay open until December 31.
  • XMR will also stop being accepted as collateral for VIP loans, so borrowers may need to add other collateral to avoid liquidation.
  • KuCoin is the most active XMR venue (about $62.6 million in 24-hour volume on XMR/USDT per CoinGecko), following MEXC, Binance and Kraken EEA exits.
  • The network does not depend on KuCoin, but liquidity does: watch where volume migrates and how much slippage the remaining exchanges show.

Monero (XMR) lost around 15% of its value in less than five hours on Thursday after KuCoin announced plans to remove the privacy coin from its platform. The decision comes just nine days after rival exchange MEXC discontinued XMR spot trading, leaving investors with fewer options to trade one of the cryptocurrency market’s largest privacy-focused assets.

Data from BitInfoCharts shows that Monero fell from $525.36 to $446.54 during Thursday’s trading session. For longtime XMR investors, the sell-off is an uncomfortable reminder of what happened when Binance announced its Monero delisting in February 2024.

This time, however, the list of major exchanges available to Monero traders is considerably shorter.

KuCoin Gives Monero Traders Four Days Before Trading Ends

In a November 26 announcement, KuCoin confirmed that it will remove all four Monero spot trading pairs against USDT, USDC, ETH and BTC on November 30 at 08:00 UTC.

The exchange has already suspended XMR deposits and does not intend to reopen them. Withdrawals are scheduled to remain available until December 31 at 08:00 UTC, although KuCoin reserves the right to close them earlier if problems affecting the network arise.

Monero’s removal extends beyond spot trading. KuCoin will discontinue XMR flexible savings on November 27, followed by its conversion and automated trading services on November 30.

There is another detail in the announcement that deserves particular attention. KuCoin will stop accepting XMR as collateral for its VIP loan products. Customers who have borrowed against their Monero holdings may need to provide alternative collateral to avoid liquidation.

For holders planning to leave their coins on the exchange until the withdrawal deadline, KuCoin also warned that remaining balances could be converted into stablecoins, although “such conversion is not guaranteed.”

The exchange cited its platform policies but did not identify a specific regulatory requirement behind the decision.

Monero’s Liquidity Problem Is Getting Harder To Ignore

KuCoin is not the first exchange to abandon Monero this month, but its departure could prove particularly significant given the amount of XMR trading it handles.

A November 26 snapshot from CoinGecko identified KuCoin as Monero’s most active exchange, with its XMR/USDT pair recording approximately $62.6 million in trading volume over a 24-hour period.

Earlier this month, MEXC discontinued spot trading for Monero on November 17. Binance removed the cryptocurrency in February 2024, while Kraken halted XMR trading for European Economic Area customers in October of the same year, explicitly citing regulatory changes.

Kaiko’s historical research illustrates how liquidity across privacy cryptocurrencies had already deteriorated by early 2024, following a series of exchange restrictions.

Trading volume does not simply disappear when an exchange delists an asset. Some of it will move elsewhere, and investors who intend to keep their holdings can withdraw them to private wallets.

The bigger question is how efficiently the remaining exchanges can absorb that activity. If fewer venues are competing for the same orders, particularly during periods of market stress, large trades could become more expensive to execute and price swings more pronounced.

For Monero, that is increasingly a market structure problem rather than a question of whether its underlying technology works.

Can XMR Survive Another Major Exchange Exit?

There is a case against assuming that Thursday’s sell-off marks the beginning of a prolonged decline.

Monero has survived previous exchange removals and even managed to establish new price highs in 2026 despite mounting restrictions. As NewsBTC previously reported, XMR traded above $700 earlier this year, long after Binance stopped supporting its spot markets.

The cryptocurrency’s network does not depend on KuCoin to process transactions. Its utility as a privacy-focused payment system remains separate from its availability on centralized trading platforms.

But a functioning network does not guarantee a liquid market. Investors still need practical ways to enter and exit their positions without incurring excessive trading costs.

November 30 will therefore be an important test for Monero. Rather than focusing solely on whether XMR recovers the $500 level, traders should watch where KuCoin’s trading volume migrates and whether the remaining exchanges can absorb larger orders without substantial slippage.

That will offer a better indication of whether Thursday’s decline was a temporary reaction to another delisting or a warning of a deeper liquidity problem.

title: Bitcoin (BTC) Price Today: Whale Selling Near $60K Adds to Glassnode’s Warning for Wall Street
summary: Bitcoin traded near $60,000 on Thursday as whale distribution and weak demand added pressure to a market already struggling to regain its footing.
content:
Skip to content
Assets: BTC

Bitcoin traded near $60,000 on Thursday as whale distribution and weak demand added pressure to a market already struggling to regain its footing.

BTC recovered toward $60,400 on November 26 after falling to approximately $57,900 a day earlier. However, recent on-chain data suggests that selling pressure among large holders remains a concern for the market.

Santiment’s latest figures show that wallets holding between 10 and 10,000 BTC have reduced their combined balances by approximately 150,000 coins since November 2. Meanwhile, Glassnode warns that Bitcoin’s weakness could signal broader risk aversion across traditional financial markets.

Bitcoin Whales Reduce Holdings by 150K BTC

Santiment data shows that addresses holding between 10 and 10,000 BTC reduced their combined balances by around 150,000 BTC, representing a 1.1% decline since November 2. Their holdings fell from approximately 13.73 million BTC to 13.58 million BTC.

Bitcoin holdings have declined from their November 2 peak of 13.73 million BTC, suggesting continued selling pressure could prolong correction risks until accumulation resumes. Source: Santiment Intelligence via X

The distribution occurred as Bitcoin’s price declined 24.5%, falling from approximately $76,700 to $57,900 over the same period. Despite the reduction, this wallet cohort still controls around 67.55% of Bitcoin’s total circulating supply, making its accumulation and distribution patterns important indicators of market sentiment.

The data points to weakening conviction among a substantial group of Bitcoin holders. Continued balance reductions could increase the amount of available supply in the market, particularly when demand from new buyers remains limited.

However, changes in wallet balances do not establish the destination of every transferred coin or confirm that every movement represents an outright sale. The figures are best viewed as evidence of distribution within a defined wallet-size cohort.

A sustained reversal in this trend could provide a different signal. Stabilizing balances followed by renewed accumulation would suggest that these holders are becoming more comfortable with Bitcoin’s price levels.

Glassnode Sees Bitcoin Flashing a Warning for Wall Street

Glassnode’s latest market assessment highlights Bitcoin’s relative weakness following news that NVIDIA reinstated Jensen Huang as its CEO, less than two weeks after his resignation.

The announcement initially triggered a rally across financial markets. Bitcoin gained approximately 5% in around 30 minutes alongside equities. However, the move quickly faded, with BTC giving back its entire advance in less than six hours. The Nasdaq 100, meanwhile, retained roughly three-quarters of its initial gain during that period.

Bitcoin led the market decline with a 5.5% drop, followed by the Nasdaq at 3.1% and the S&P 500 at 1.3%, while NVIDIA briefly rallied before retreating. Source: Glassnode via X

Glassnode described Bitcoin as the “canary in the coal mine,” arguing that its continuous trading makes it one of the first assets to reflect changing investor risk appetite. The research firm noted that stocks reacted more slowly but subsequently came under pressure as most of the Nasdaq’s initial gains disappeared.

The relationship between Bitcoin and traditional equities has also strengthened. According to Glassnode, the correlation between BTC and the Nasdaq 100 reached its highest level since September 2022, during the previous bear market.

This relationship matters because Bitcoin’s recovery could become more difficult if equity markets continue weakening. Glassnode also found that BTC has recently underperformed the Nasdaq on both positive and negative trading sessions, rising less when equities advance and falling more during declines.

Institutional demand presents another concern. Glassnode reported that US spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded approximately $4.3 billion in net outflows over 20 trading days. Coinbase spot trading also showed persistent net selling among market takers over the previous 30 days.

These figures suggest that the US institutional buying interest that supported Bitcoin during its previous advance has weakened. A return of ETF inflows and stronger spot buying could provide evidence that demand is recovering.

$16B in Short Liquidations Could Fuel a Bitcoin Rebound

Despite the pressure from whale distribution and institutional outflows, Bitcoin’s derivatives market presents a potentially different picture.

CryptoQuant CEO Ki Young Ju highlighted an imbalance between potential short and long liquidations. According to his November 26 assessment, approximately $16 billion in short positions could face liquidation as BTC moves through the $60,000-$100,000 range. Potential long liquidations below $60,000, meanwhile, total less than $5 billion.

The chart highlights concentrated short liquidation exposure above $60,000, while long liquidation exposure at lower price levels remains limited. Source: Ki Young Ju via X

Ju stated that “The squeeze risk is on the short side,” pointing to the growing concentration of bearish leveraged positions.

A short squeeze occurs when rising prices force traders betting against an asset to close their positions. These traders may need to buy back Bitcoin to cover their exposure, potentially adding further upward pressure to the price.

The estimated liquidation imbalance could therefore create conditions for an accelerated recovery if Bitcoin attracts sufficient buying interest. However, the figures represent potential exposure rather than guaranteed liquidations. Price must reach the relevant liquidation levels before those positions are forced to close.

This distinction is important given the broader market environment. A concentration of short positions alone cannot reverse persistent spot selling or compensate for weakening demand. Bitcoin would still need sustained buying activity to establish a stronger upward trend.

Bitcoin’s 411-Day Decline Raises Questions About the Four-Year Cycle

Bitcoin’s longer-term performance also raises questions about whether its historical market cycle pattern will continue.

A recent CryptoQuant analysis compared the current downturn with previous Bitcoin cycles. The period from October 6, 2025, to November 21, 2026, spans 411 days, broadly matching the duration of several historical one-year declines.

Historical cycles show varying correction depths, with the 2026 downturn appearing severe, but past patterns alone do not confirm a market bottom without renewed demand. Source: CryptoQuant via X

The comparison has renewed attention on the familiar market pattern often described as “one year down, three years up.” Previous cycles showed lengthy recovery phases following deep corrections, but their timing does not establish a reliable schedule for future price movements.

The current drawdown also requires additional confirmation before it can be considered complete. CryptoQuant’s apparent demand indicators show both the 30-day and one-year metrics remaining below zero, suggesting that underlying demand has not recovered sufficiently.

Apparent demand estimates the relationship between new Bitcoin issuance and changes in the supply of coins that have remained inactive for more than a year. It provides insight into demand conditions but does not directly measure total spot purchases or net investment flows.

CryptoQuant’s analysis identifies a sustained improvement in this metric as an important condition for recovery. Stronger spot buying and renewed Bitcoin ETF inflows would also help demonstrate that buyers are absorbing available supply.

The analysis cautions against treating historical similarities as confirmation of a market bottom. As the contributor noted, “A durable recovery requires buyers willing to absorb supply.”

Bitcoin (BTC) Price Analysis

Bitcoin’s position around $60,000 remains an important test following its recent decline. Glassnode previously identified the $62,000-$66,000 region as a support area. However, BTC closed below this range on November 19, turning the previous support zone into potential resistance.

Bitcoin (BTC) price chart. Source: Brave New Coin

The cryptocurrency subsequently fell to approximately $55,300 on November 21 before recovering toward $60,000. Glassnode identified $58,500, corresponding to the June low, as another important level to monitor.

A convincing daily close below $60,000, followed by a break beneath $58,500, could expose Bitcoin to further downside. Glassnode placed its realized price—the average price at which coins last moved on-chain—near $53,200 as a potential lower reference level. This remains a conditional scenario rather than a confirmed price target.

On the upside, reclaiming the $62,000-$66,000 region would help improve Bitcoin’s immediate market structure. However, sustained recovery would require more than a short squeeze. Reduced whale distribution, stronger spot demand, and improving ETF flows would provide more meaningful evidence of a developing trend reversal.

For now, Bitcoin faces competing signals. The derivatives market shows considerable potential short-liquidation exposure, while on-chain distribution and weakening institutional demand continue to challenge recovery prospects. Whether BTC can stabilize near $60,000 may depend on whether fresh buyers emerge to absorb the available supply.

title: PEPE Whales Are Sitting On $21 Million In Tokens, And One Wallet Keeps Getting Bigger
summary: Key takeaways Lookonchain reports PEPE whales hold more than six trillion tokens, about $21.16 million, most of it in one wallet (0x5011) that has been buying since November 17. That wallet holds 5.15 trillion PEPE, roughly $18.28 million and about 1.22% of total supply; a second wallet (0x6246) hol...
content:
Key takeaways

  • Lookonchain reports PEPE whales hold more than six trillion tokens, about $21.16 million, most of it in one wallet (0x5011) that has been buying since November 17.
  • That wallet holds 5.15 trillion PEPE, roughly $18.28 million and about 1.22% of total supply; a second wallet (0x6246) holds 868.16 billion PEPE, about $2.88 million.
  • Not all large holders agree: Deep Blue Alpha data shows withdrawals were only about 36% of tracked whale transfers over seven days, so exchange deposits outweighed them.
  • Exchange deposits are not necessarily sales, and withdrawals do not prove a fresh purchase.
  • At this size, exiting at the quoted price depends on liquidity; a $0.000001 price move changes a 5.15 trillion position by $5.15 million.

PEPE whales have accumulated more than six trillion tokens worth approximately $21.16 million, according to new data from blockchain monitoring platform Lookonchain. Most of that position belongs to a single unidentified wallet that has been accumulating the memecoin since November 17.

The size of the position is unusual even by memecoin standards. One address now holds more than 1% of PEPE’s entire supply, and its owner has continued adding tokens despite weakness in the market.

A Mystery PEPE Whale Keeps Adding To Its Position

The wallet, identified by its opening characters 0x5011, accumulated 5.15 trillion PEPE over eight days. Lookonchain valued the holdings at $18.28 million, representing approximately 1.22% of the cryptocurrency’s total supply.

The more interesting detail is how quickly the position has grown.

Lookonchain’s transaction monitoring history shows that by November 19, the wallet had withdrawn around 1.9 trillion PEPE from Binance. That figure climbed to 2.878 trillion by November 23 and exceeded 3.3 trillion the following day.

On Wednesday, Lookonchain reported that the address had accumulated 4.16 trillion tokens. By Thursday, its reported holdings had reached 5.15 trillion.

Another wallet, beginning with 0x6246, accumulated 868.16 billion PEPE valued at approximately $2.88 million, bringing the combined reported value to more than $21 million.

Large withdrawals are nothing new for the memecoin. NewsBTC previously covered a separate PEPE whale moving $14.7 million out of Binance. What makes the latest activity particularly interesting is the repeated accumulation within such a short period.

The Other Side Of The PEPE Whale Trade

Before treating these transactions as a bullish signal, it’s worth looking at what other large holders have been doing.

Data from blockchain analytics platform Deep Blue Alpha showed that withdrawals accounted for approximately 36% of tracked PEPE whale transfers between wallets and exchanges over the preceding seven days, according to its November 26 update.

In other words, exchange deposits outweighed withdrawals within that particular group of wallets.

That doesn’t invalidate Lookonchain’s findings. It does, however, complicate the idea that large investors are collectively preparing for a PEPE recovery.

One group of holders may be increasing its exposure while others are looking to reduce theirs. The distinction matters, especially in a market where a handful of transactions can attract more attention than the activity of dozens of other wallets.

Exchange deposits aren’t necessarily sales, just as withdrawals don’t establish that a fresh purchase has taken place. Centralized exchange trading records remain largely invisible to outside observers.

What A Trillion-Token Position Means For PEPE

For an investor holding 5.15 trillion PEPE, even a movement of $0.000001 in the token’s price would change the value of the position by $5.15 million.

That illustrates both the attraction and the risk of holding such a large quantity of a speculative asset.

Building an $18 million position is one thing. Exiting it at the quoted market price is another. The amount an investor can actually realize depends on available liquidity, execution and the market’s ability to absorb the tokens.

Concentrated holdings can therefore work in both directions. If tokens remain outside exchanges, they may reduce the supply immediately available for trading. If the same tokens return to exchanges, traders may suddenly find themselves watching for potential selling pressure.

The next development worth following is whether these wallets continue accumulating or begin transferring tokens back to trading platforms.

For now, two addresses hold an unusually large amount of PEPE. Whether the rest of the market shares their apparent appetite for the memecoin is a different question.
